   Option Default Choices     MODE CSV CSV, CSP, CST, CSTCA   TP 0 0 or 1; optional touch-probe status only   DIAG 0 0 or 1; actual velocity, torque and DC voltage   INFO2 NONE NONE, INPUTS, TEMP   ENC_STAT 0 0 only; EL7411 has no documented EL72xx encoder-status PDO    Channel 1 overrides (MODE_1, TP_1, DIAG_1, INFO2_1, ENC_STAT_1) follow the shared option precedence. Second-channel options are rejected. Invalid combinations fail before slave reset or hardware configuration. INFO2=ERRORS is not offered for EL7411; use the HW diagnostic-buffer button.
The default process image contains drive control, velocity demand, primary position and drive status only. Default CSP similarly matches the existing EL7411_CSP PDO set. With MODE=CSP,DIAG=1, following error is additionally mapped at 0x6010:06. Torque offset is not mapped on EL7411.
INFO2=INPUTS uses a separate EL7411 record template: its hardware-enable/STO input level is bit 12, whereas the EL72xx template uses bit 8. The shared inputs panel displays that level through Drv01-STO01; this is a diagnostic input level, not a complete safety-state assessment. The Info2 selector SDO 0x8010:3A is a UINT8 and is written as a one-byte value.
CSTCA target and readbacks CSTCA uses target torque plus an externally commanded electrical angle. The startup SDO 0x7010:03 is set to 11. CSV, CSP and CST use 9, 8 and 10.
   Logical EtherCAT entry PDO Object Type     torqueSetpoint01 0x1602 0x7010:09 S16   commutationAngle01 0x1603 0x7010:0E U16    The following PV suffixes use the normal slave prefix $(IOC):m$(MasterID)s$(SlaveID)-:
   Writable target Demand readback Units     Drv01-Trq Drv01-Trq-RB Percent, 0.1 per raw count   Drv01-ComAngle Drv01-ComAngle-RB Electrical degrees, 360/65536 per raw count    The angle target is bounded to 0…359.9945068359375 degrees, corresponding to raw U16 values 0…65535. The angle readback reports the commanded PDO value; it is not a measured rotor angle. CSTCA controls the electrical angle directly, so it can produce motor movement when enabled.
Panels The wrapper uses the existing 128 × 500 OPT overview, including its HW EtherCAT diagnostic-buffer shortcut. CfgMode=3 identifies CSTCA; CSV/CSP/CST retain values 0/1/2. The channel panel shows a CSTCA details link only when that mode is configured. The EL/EP/ELM72xx wrappers also support CSTCA, with a different input PDO policy.
ecmcEX72XX_OPT_cstca.ui provides torque controls and a writable angle, angle demand readback and > trend button in a compact 350 × 332 panel. Press Enter to write torque or angle. With DIAG=1, actual torque is also shown. With DIAG=0, it displays Not mapped and does not subscribe to an absent actual-torque PV. DS402 enable/disable and the state guide remain available without an axis object. Coordinate direct target writes with the axis configuration whenever an axis controls the drive.
CSV/CSP/CST, diagnostics, touch-probe and temperature panels are shared with Ex72xx OPT. Velocity and position demand records default to the legacy raw scale (1, RAW). VEL_ESLO, VEL_EGU, POS_ESLO and POS_EGU can override demand/velocity record scaling; they do not change the drive’s SDO scaling. Primary encoder position retains the existing raw-position record convention.
Timing and validation The default DC schedule and current initialization match the legacy EL7411: Sync 0 is 62500 ns, Sync 1 is the application period minus 62500 ns, both 0x1C32 and 0x1C33 receive sync-mode 3 and the application period, and the initial peak-current SDO is 1000 mA. Motor configuration can overwrite that current setting. SYNC_0_CYCLE, SYNC_0_SHIFT, SYNC_1_CYCLE, SYNC_1_SHIFT, WATCHDOG_DIVIDER and WATCHDOG_INTERVALS use the shared override conventions. No EtherCAT port-wiring check is enabled. The shared startup-delay policy is retained.
Static integration checks compare default CSV/CSP mappings to the legacy configurations, exercise all mode/feature combinations, expand databases, verify angle scaling and limits, follow visible panel links and compile the Qt panels. They do not connect to a drive; commissioning on target hardware remains necessary.
Mapping sources: Beckhoff EL7411 standard objects, configuration data, and commissioning with status word and control word.

title: EL9xxx
content:
Scope Use this page for EL9xxx supply and distribution terminals, especially over-current protection modules and passive-terminal-related slave-index confusion.
Topics  Over-current protection Passive terminals   Over-current protection In the standard setup at PSI, over-current protection modules are used to feed 24V to both the EtherCAT communication bus (E-bus) and the power bus of the EtherCAT slaves. If the over-current protection is not enabled, then the EtherCAT slaves will not receive power.
The first time (and only the first time) a system is used, the over-current modules need to be enabled in order to allow current to flow. Enabling is done by push buttons in the LED area of the module. The long horizontal LEDs are in fact buttons that can be used to activate or trip the over-current protection.
Before pressing any button, check the electrical drawings and make sure it’s safe to power on the system.
 EL9221-5000 The EL9221-5000 has one channel and therefore only the top button is needed to be pressed.
EL9227-5500 The EL9227-5500 is a 2-channel module and normally both channels need to be enabled by pressing both the top and bottom long LED. If only one is pressed, it could result in communication power being fine while power to the I/O bus is missing. This can result in strange issues. Both EL9227-5500 and EL9221-5000 have dedicated panels where over-current protection status can be seen.
Passive terminals Some terminals are passive. Passive terminals are not EtherCAT slaves and do not communicate over EtherCAT (not equipped with EtherCAT slave controller). Passive terminals are normally used to simplify electrical connections (avoiding external terminals). For instance for distributing potential, 24V and 0V, an EL9184 can be used (8Ch 24V and 8Ch 0V).
The passive terminals will not show up as an EtherCAT slave when issuing the ethercat slaves command. However, they are normally visible in the electrical drawings. This could result in the slave ID in the electrical drawing NOT corresponding to the EtherCAT slave index used when configuring ecmc. In the worst case, this could lead to the wrong hardware/drive being configured.
When configuring ecmc, make sure the EtherCAT slave index is correct. Do not blindly trust the electrical drawings since a passive terminal could introduce a shift in the slave indices.
 Related Pages  hardware ethercat command line interface

title: Ex72xx option configurations
content:
The OPT wrappers use a common dispatcher and per-channel record/panel interface, with separate PDO mappings and timing policies for EL/EP72xx and ELM72xx. All existing non-OPT hardware configurations, databases and panels are unchanged.
For the EL7411-specific mapping, defaults and CSTCA input diagnostics, see EL7411 OPT. The existing EL/EP/ELM72xx CSTCA behaviour described here is unchanged.
Devices and defaults    HW_DESC Channels PDO family Default MODE TP INFO2 DIAG     EL7211-9014_OPT 1 EL72XX CSV 1 INPUTS 1   EP7211-0034_OPT 1 EL72XX CSV 1 INPUTS 1   EL7201_OPT 1 EL72XX CSV 0 ERRORS 1   EL7201-0010_OPT 1 EL72XX CSV 1 ERRORS 1   ELM7231-0010_OPT 1 ELM72XX CSV 0 NONE 0   ELM7222-0010_OPT 2 ELM72XX CSV 0 NONE 0    The defaults retain the corresponding legacy CSV/STD mappings and logical entry names, with encoder feedback status additionally enabled on every channel. Set ENC_STAT=0 to omit that addition. The ELM defaults retain the other minimal mappings of the existing ELM CSV configs; there are no ELM STD configs in this repository. ELM channels read their electronic motor nameplates, as in the existing configurations.
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=EL7201-0010_OPT" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=EL7211-9014_OPT,OPT='MODE=CSP,ENC_STAT=1,TP=0,INFO2=TEMP'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=ELM7231-0010_OPT,OPT='MODE=CST,DIAG=1'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=ELM7222-0010_OPT,OPT='MODE_1=CSV,MODE_2=CSP,TP_2=1,DIAG_2=1,INFO2_2=TEMP'" Example: three EL7211-9014 drives This PSI engineering-startup excerpt configures three consecutive slaves on master 0: slave 36 in CST, slave 37 in CSV and slave 38 in CSP. addSlave.cmd increments SLAVE_ID after each call, so only the first position is specified. Apply the motor component immediately after each slave: it configures the most recently added drive.
require ecmccfg sandst_a "ENG_MODE=1,MASTER_ID=0,ECMC_VER=v11.1.0_RC1" #- ec0.s36: cyclic synchronous torque. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "SLAVE_ID=36,HW_DESC=EL7211-9014_OPT,OPT='MODE=CST'" #- Limit maximum current to 1355 mA: half the motor nominal current of 2710 mA. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Beckhoff-AM8111-XFX0,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=1355'" #- ec0.s37: cyclic synchronous velocity. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "HW_DESC=EL7211-9014_OPT,OPT='MODE=CSV'" #- Limit maximum current to 1355 mA: half the motor nominal current of 2710 mA. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Beckhoff-AM8111-XFX0,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=1355'" #- ec0.s38: cyclic synchronous position. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "HW_DESC=EL7211-9014_OPT,OPT='MODE=CSP'" #- Limit maximum current to 1355 mA: half the motor nominal current of 2710 mA. ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Beckhoff-AM8111-XFX0,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=1355'" The sandst_a module build and v11.1.0_RC1 version are specific to this example’s environment. applyComponent.cmd requires access to ecmccomp. Use the normal IOC startup sequence to apply the completed bus configuration.
The AM8111-XFX0 component defines nominal current as 2710 mA. I_MAX_MA=1355 overrides the maximum-current setting; the nominal-current setting remains 2710 mA. All three profiles retain the default ENC_STAT=1, TP=1, INFO2=INPUTS and DIAG=1.
Options and capabilities MODE accepts CSV, CSP, CST or CSTCA for every wrapper. Each channel explicitly selects its mode by a one-byte startup SDO: CSV = 9, CSP = 8, CST = 10, CSTCA = 11. Channel 1 uses 0x7010:03; ELM channel 2 uses 0x7110:03.
TP accepts 0 or 1 and maps touch-probe status, including input levels. EL7201 with resolver feedback does not support this option; TP=1 is rejected. Other wrappers support it. Touch-probe control and captured positions are not part of this option.
DIAG=1 maps actual velocity, actual torque and DC link voltage, and loads their records. DIAG=0 omits them. ELM CSP additionally maps following error when DIAG=1. EL/EP CSP always maps following error, as in CSP_STD. EL/EP CSV and CSP map torque offset; ELM does not map torque offset. CST and CSTCA use torque demand. ENC_STAT=1 is the default on every listed wrapper in CSV, CSP and CST. CSTCA omits feedback PDOs regardless of this option. It maps encoder feedback status and loads its records. ENC_STAT=0 omits the PDO and records; ENC_STAT_1 / ENC_STAT_2 can override each channel separately. CfgEncoderStatus and the panel link reflect the resolved selection.
EL/EP use PDO 0x1A0C; ELM uses 0x1A02 for channel 1 and 0x1A42 for channel 2. Each carries the same 16-bit layout: padding in bits 0–12, position-invalid in bit 13, and the input cycle counter in bits 14–15. The shared records retain encoderStatus01/02, Enc01/02-Stat and Enc01/02-NotValid.
   INFO2 Meaning Supported wrappers     INPUTS Digital inputs 1/2 and STO, selection 10 EL7211-9014, EP7211-0034   TEMP PCB temperature, selection 4 All listed wrappers   ERRORS Raw drive error bitmap, selection 5 EL/EP wrappers   NONE Omit Info2 PDO and records All listed wrappers    Velocity/position demand records and velocity diagnostics use the EL STD scaling on EL/EP (2.3406E-5, rad/s). ELM retains the existing raw demand convention (1, RAW), also used for its optional velocity diagnostics. VEL_ESLO, VEL_EGU, POS_ESLO and POS_EGU override record scaling/units when needed for the drive’s configured scaling. They do not change drive SDO scaling. Torque records use 0.1 percent per count in both families.
The ELM INPUTS selection is deliberately not exposed through the STO-oriented input template. Use TP=1 for the two touch-probe input levels. Error bitmap records expose the raw word; interpreting individual bits requires the matching drive revision’s documentation.
MODE_1, TP_1, INFO2_1, DIAG_1 and ENC_STAT_1 override the shared option for channel 1. ELM7222 also accepts the corresponding _2 overrides. A channel-specific value wins over the shared value, which wins over the wrapper default. Second-channel options on a single-channel wrapper are rejected. All channels are validated before resetting or configuring the slave. No ecmcIf state is used.
CSTCA: external commutation angle Select MODE=CSTCA to send torque and the electrical commutation angle over EtherCAT. MODE_1=CSTCA and MODE_2=CSTCA select it independently on ELM7222.
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=EL7211-9014_OPT,OPT='MODE=CSTCA'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=ELM7222-0010_OPT,OPT='MODE_1=CST,MODE_2=CSTCA'" CSTCA uses a minimal TxPDO configuration: only 0x1A01 DRV Statusword on EL/EP, plus 0x1A05 Info2 inputs when INFO2=INPUTS is selected on a supported wrapper. INFO2=NONE selects statusword only. ELM uses its corresponding drive statusword PDO (0x1A10 / 0x1A50); ELM does not support INFO2=INPUTS. Position feedback, encoder status, touch probe, velocity, torque and voltage telemetry are omitted in CSTCA, even when ENC_STAT, TP or DIAG are enabled. INFO2=TEMP and INFO2=ERRORS are also omitted in this mode. Configuration PVs report the effective selection, and position widgets and unavailable feature links are hidden. Other channels retain their own selected mode’s mappings.
The torque PDO and Drv01-Trq / Drv01-Trq-RB records are shared with CST. CSTCA additionally maps commutationAngle01 (commutationAngle02 on channel 2) as UINT16 at 0x7010:0E (0x7110:0E). EL/EP use RxPDO 0x1603; ELM uses 0x1614 / 0x1654. Other modes do not map this output.
Drv01-ComAngle is writable in electrical degrees; Drv01-ComAngle-RB reads back the PDO demand, not a measured rotor angle. Channel 2 uses Drv02. The scale is 360/65536 degrees per count, with a writable range of 0 through 359.9945068359375 degrees. Real-time logic can write the raw commutationAngle01/02 entry in counts (0–65535). The controller supplies the angle cyclically when running external commutation; the EPICS record is a manual setpoint. The CSTCA detail panel includes torque controls and the angle setpoint/readback. CfgMode=3 selects that panel.
Sources: EL output objects, EP output objects, ELM output objects, and the family PDO references below.
Timing and startup policy    Setting EL7211-9014 / EP7211-0034 / EL7201-0010 EL7201 resolver ELM72xx     Sync0 period EtherCAT cycle EtherCAT cycle 62500 ns   Sync0 shift 0 Half EtherCAT cycle ECMC_SYNC_0_OFFSET_NS, default 0   Sync1 period 0 0 EtherCAT cycle   Sync1 shift 0 0 ECMC_SYNC_1_OFFSET_NS, default 0   Initial peak-current SDO 100 mA, motor config overwrites it Same Nameplate policy; no EL peak-current override    EtherCAT port-wiring checks are enabled by the EP wrapper only. EL and ELM wrappers do not enable this check.
All wrappers accept SYNC_0_CYCLE, SYNC_0_SHIFT, SYNC_1_CYCLE and SYNC_1_SHIFT overrides in ns. ELM timing does not issue EL-specific 0x1C32:02 and 0x1C33:02 cycle-time SDOs. The watchdog helper retains its sample-rate-based defaults and accepts WATCHDOG_DIVIDER and WATCHDOG_INTERVALS. The existing ECMC_EC_STARTUP_DELAY_EL72XX startup-delay setting is retained.
Extending a family Device wrappers fix product identity, family, channel count, capabilities and defaults. ecmcEX72XX_OPT.cmd validates channels before slave reset, dispatches the mappings and applies the family’s timing policy.
 ecmcEX72XX_OPT_EL72XX_pdo.cmd and _timing.cmd implement EL/EP policy. ecmcEX72XX_OPT_ELM72XX_pdo.cmd and _timing.cmd implement ELM policy, including the second channel’s PDO and object offsets. ecmcEX72XX_OPT_channel.cmd shares mode SDO selection, feature records and configuration readbacks across families.  The mapping preserves common logical entry names such as driveControl01, velocitySetpoint01 and positionActual01. ELM channel 2 uses suffix 02. The EL7201-0010 following-error object uses subindex 0x06; the existing EL7211-9014/EP7211-0034 STD mapping uses 0x09.
These wrappers support the MDP742 layout only. DS402-profile device variants need their own family mapping and are not aliases for these wrappers. Likewise, adding another ELM or EL variant requires checking its exact ESI/revision and capabilities; the family name alone does not establish compatibility.
References: EL OCT PDO mapping, EL resolver mapping, ELM PDO mapping, ELM input objects, MDP742 versus DS402.
Panels and records Single-channel wrappers select ecmcEX72XX_OPT.ui. ELM7222 selects the dedicated ecmcEX72XX_OPT_2ch.ui top-level overview. Both keep the standard 128 x 500 slave frame and the IOC, MasterID and SlaveID macros.
The two-channel overview shows each channel’s mode, encoder position, decoded DS402 state and Fault/Warning LEDs, with equal links to open channel 1 or channel 2. It does not embed one channel’s detailed controls. Each link opens the shared channel panel with its own explicit ChID, CfgSuffix and ChannelTitle macros. The single-channel overview passes an empty title; two-channel subpanels show Channel 1 or Channel 2.
The channel panel’s Drive tab groups motion mode, encoder position, drive state, Fault/Warning LEDs and configured drive-detail links. The Setup tab groups touch-probe and Info2 configuration readbacks and their detail links.
caQtDM -macro 'IOC=IOC_PREFIX,MasterID=0,SlaveID=1' ecmcEX72XX_OPT.ui caQtDM -macro 'IOC=IOC_PREFIX,MasterID=0,SlaveID=1' ecmcEX72XX_OPT_2ch.ui Configuration PVs use the slave’s ECMC_P, normally $(IOC):m$(MasterID)s$(SlaveID)-:
   Suffix Values     CfgChannels 1 or 2   CfgMode 0 = CSV, 1 = CSP, 2 = CST, 3 = CSTCA   CfgTouchProbe 0 = Not mapped, 1 = Mapped   CfgInfo2 0 = INPUTS, 1 = TEMP, 2 = ERRORS, 3 = NONE   CfgDiagnostics 0 = Not mapped, 1 = Mapped   CfgTorqueOffset 0 = Not mapped, 1 = Mapped   CfgFollowingError 0 = Not mapped, 1 = Mapped   CfgEncoderStatus 0 = Not mapped, 1 = Mapped    Channel 2 adds 02 to each per-channel configuration suffix (for example CfgMode02 and CfgInfo202). These are startup readbacks; changing options requires restarting the IOC. Feature links appear only when the relevant PDOs and records are configured. Hidden links subscribe to configuration PVs only; feature records are subscribed when their detail panel is opened. A connection failure remains a connection failure, rather than implying a disabled feature. CSV, CSP, CST and CSTCA detail panels expose DS402 enable and Disable buttons. From the overview, open the desired channel and select its mode’s detail link. The buttons process that channel’s Drv01-TrgDS402Ena.PROC and Drv01-TrgDS402Dis.PROC records (channel 2 uses Drv02). The enable sequence writes control words 128, 6, 7 and 15 with fixed 10 ms delays; disable writes 0. These are direct PDO controls and require no axis object. The sequence uses fixed delays rather than waiting for status transitions; the panel displays the status word, warning and error readbacks alongside the controls.
All mode detail panels use a compact 350 x 260 layout with writable target and separate PDO demand readback:
   Mode Writable PV suffix Demand readback     CSV Drv01-Spd Drv01-Spd-RB   CSP Drv01-PosCmd Drv01-PosCmd-RB   CST Drv01-Trq Drv01-Trq-RB   CSTCA Drv01-Trq, Drv01-ComAngle Drv01-Trq-RB, Drv01-ComAngle-RB    The torque-offset detail panel also has a writable target, Drv01-TrqOff, and a separate Drv01-TrqOff-RB readback with a trend button. Enter the offset in percent and press Enter to write. This link is available for the EL72XX PDO family (EL/EP) in CSV and CSP, where the offset is mapped. The current ELM72XX and 7062 OPT configurations do not map a torque offset.
The CST panel also shows actual torque (Drv01-TrqAct / Drv02-TrqAct), in percent, alongside the demand readback. It uses the existing DIAG=1 telemetry; with DIAG=0 the panel says Not mapped and does not subscribe to that absent record. Both readbacks fit on one row, retaining the 350 x 260 panel size.
Channel 2 uses Drv02. Enter the target in the record’s configured units and press Enter to write. Torque is in percent; velocity and position use the scaling described above. These records do not require an axis object. When an axis controls the drive, use the axis panel for motion commands.
Small > buttons beside readbacks open the existing ecmcGraph_v1.ui trend panel, using the same IOC, TITLE and PV macros as the MO7221 panels. They are available for actual position in the channel/two-channel overviews, actual torque, velocity and DC link voltage in Diagnostics, CST torque demand readback and actual torque, CSP position demand readback, CSV velocity demand readback, following error, PCB temperature, and torque offset readback. Each graph targets the selected channel’s exact readback PV. Links are available only for mapped features; DIAG=0 does not offer trends for absent diagnostic records. Panel dimensions are unchanged.
DS402 state and LEDs The detail panels show Drv01-DS402State (channel 2: Drv02-DS402State), decoded from the existing status PDO. Ready, On, Enabled, Fault and Warning use LEDs instead of long binary readback strings. Hover over an LED for its bit meaning; open State guide for a compact reference to all states. Warning is a separate bit and can coexist with Operation enabled.
   Decoded state Meaning     Not ready to switch on Drive is initializing.   Switch on disabled Output stage is disabled.   Ready to switch on Shutdown command accepted.   Switched on Ready for operation enable.   Operation enabled Accepts the selected mode’s setpoint.   Quick stop active Handling a quick-stop request.   Fault reaction active Executing its fault response.   Fault Fault response complete; resolve cause.   Unknown Status bits do not match a defined state.    The decoder uses the DS402 state-bit patterns, ignoring voltage, warning and mode/manufacturer-specific bits. See the manufacturer reference for state coding.
The new OPT-only derived records refresh locally at 10 Hz and propagate invalid source alarms. They add no PDOs or SDOs. Reload the IOC database/restart the IOC to load them before using the new state readback. The existing enable sequence still uses fixed delays rather than waiting for decoded state transitions.
The encoder-status panel uses a 180 x 126 layout with a Position valid LED: green when status bit 13 is 0, red when it is 1. The two blue/grey Cycle [1:0] LEDs show the counter MSB on the left (bit 15) and LSB on the right (bit 14). The counter advances each process-data cycle and wraps from 3 to 0; it may look static at GUI sampling rates and is not a standstill/communication-health indicator. Bits 0–12 are padding, with no additional encoder diagnostics in this PDO. The raw word remains available below the LEDs, and tooltips explain each field. See the feedback-status layout and feedback validity/counter meanings.
Input/STO and touch-probe panels use compact 180 x 126 layouts. Input LEDs are green for high and grey for low. The STO OK LED is green for feedback OK (1) and red for STO active (0). Tooltips explain the colors. The touch-probe panel retains the raw status word below its two input LEDs.
Temperature records now consistently use the drive channel, for example Drv01-TmpAct or Drv02-TmpAct, backed by temperatureActual01/02. The earlier EP-specific panels and substitutions remain intact, but the EP OPT wrapper selects the shared resources.
Validation Run python3 tests/test_ex72xx_opt.py. The tests cover default PDO compatibility with legacy scripts plus the enabled encoder-status PDO, supported option combinations, independent ELM channels, mode-selection SDOs, native EPICS decoding of every 16-bit statusword, writable target PVs, timing/watchdog defaults and overrides, invalid-option rejection before reset, database expansion, record sources and visible panel channels. Database expansion needs EPICS msi; UI compilation needs Qt uic. Those checks are skipped individually if the respective tool is unavailable.
Before deployment, check EtherCAT OP, live Channel Access readbacks and panel behaviour on the actual device/revision. Static checks do not establish hardware PDO acceptance, drive mode transitions or live panel behaviour.
Related Pages  EL72xx diagnostics and troubleshooting Hardware knowledge base

title: Motor Record
content:
Scope This page covers motion topics related to the EPICS motor record in ecmccfg.
Read this page when:
 you use the motor record on a motion axis you want auto save restore of motor position you want retry behavior based on another readback source you want to disable the motor record for a specific axis  For YAML configuration of the motor record itself, see yaml configuration. For example-driven setups, see motor record examples.
Native target-write mode The native target-position interface can optionally start ABS/REL motion on a write, similar to writing motor-record .VAL. With this mode enabled, the axis can move without a separate EXECUTE request, including automatic drive enable when configured. It is disabled by default and does not change the motor record’s own .VAL behavior. See Native target-write motion for the commands and the NO EXEC panel indication.
Common use cases Auto save restore Open-loop stepper systems with incremental encoders often use auto save restore through the motor record. For soft-limit restoration, the exact driver option, value precedence, startup gate and position policy, see motor position and soft-limit autosave.
Important note:
 this position-restore workflow is intended for incremental encoders in YAML terms this means encoder.type: 0 soft-limit restoration is independent of position restoration; see the autosave guide  At PSI, this is commonly done by adding a file ending in _pos.req in the local cfg/ directory and listing the DVAL fields that should be restored.
Example:
MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DVAL Both autosave passes, 0 and 1, must be registered before iocInit. In the PSI ioc install workflow, a _pos.req filename selects the two-pass setup. For another filename, request it explicitly with the PSI directive below (the value 2 is not an autosave pass number):
#ENABLE-PASS=2 MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DVAL Open-loop retries based on another readback Another common use case is open-loop motion with retries based on an absolute encoder or another EPICS readback source.
Typical setup:
 one encoder is used for the axis control path another readback PV is connected to the motor record retry logic the motor record retries until the readback is within the retry deadband  This is the pattern used in the open-loop retry examples.
Useful motor-record fields These fields are often relevant in retry-based setups:
 RTRY: max retry count RMOD: retry mode UEIP: use encoder if present RDBD: retry deadband URIP: use RDBL link if present RDBL: readback link  RTRY Maximum retry count. Must be greater than zero to enable retry behavior.
RMOD Retry mode:
 0: Unity 1: Arithmetic 2: Geometric 3: In-Position  For retry tests, modes 1 and 2 are the normal choices.
UEIP Use encoder if present. In the retry example this is normally set to 0.
RDBD Retry deadband. If the readback is outside this band, another move is started.
URIP Use RDBL if present. Set this to 1 when the retry logic should use the linked readback PV.
RDBL Readback link used by the motor record retry logic. This can be any EPICS PV. In practice it is often linked to another encoder readback.
Setting fields from YAML Additional motor-record fields can be set through epics.motorRecord.fieldInit.
Example:
epics: name: ${AX_NAME=M1} precision: 3 description: Test cfg unit: mm motorRecord: fieldInit: 'FOFF=Frozen,RRES=1.0,RTRY=2,RMOD=1,UEIP=0,RDBD=0.1,URIP=1,RDBL=$(IOC):${AX_NAME=M1}-Enc${RTRY_ENC_CH=01}-PosAct'  Do not use CP on the RDBL link in this workflow.
 Running a retry-based test Typical sequence:
 start the IOC write a target position to the motor record observe the move and retry behavior until the linked readback is within deadband  Example:
dbpf IOC_TEST:Axis1 10 Expected result in the retry example:
 ecmc axis actual position ends at the open-loop equivalent value motor record position ends at the requested target  Jogging is generally not supported in this retry-based setup.
Low-level motor-controller iocsh commands Most ecmccfg users do not need to call the low-level motor-record iocsh commands directly, because the startup scripts and YAML loaders do that work.
The underlying motor layer in ecmc also registers:
ecmcMotorRecordCreateController(<port>, <not_used>, <not_used>, <movingPollMs>, <idlePollMs>, <options>) ecmcMotorRecordCreateAxis(<controllerPort>, <axisNo>, <axisFlags>, <axisOptions>) These are relevant mainly when:
 bringing up raw ecmc without the normal ecmccfg startup flow debugging the motor-record layer itself working directly with custom controller/axis creation outside the YAML and classic wrappers  For PVT/profile-move specific direct commands, see PVT.
Alarm behavior on RDBL If the RDBL PV goes into MAJOR or INVALID alarm, the motor record stops motion independent of severity propagation settings.
This is useful for protective interlocking, but it also means that badly chosen alarm limits on the linked readback can stop motion unexpectedly.
This is especially relevant if the linked value is derived from an incremental encoder or a calculated signal that can leave the normal operating range during homing or switch events.
Temporarily bypassing the RDBL interlock If motion is blocked by the RDBL alarm path, the retry link can be disabled by setting URIP to 0:
dbpf IOC_TEST:Axis1.URIP 0 Motion can then continue, but retries based on RDBL are disabled while this setting is active.
Related examples  auto save restore: examples/PSI/best_practice/motion/stepper_openloop_asr/ open loop retries: examples/PSI/best_practice/motion/stepper_openloop_mr_rtry_bissc/ no motor record: examples/PSI/best_practice/motion/stepper_bissc_no_mr/

title: Beckhoff MX-System
content:
MO1008, MO2008 and MO2338 connector variants For MO1008, MO2008 and MO2338, the -1111 and -1112 suffixes select the connector type. Both variants use the same PDO configuration, database records and panel. The suffix is optional when selecting the hardware configuration:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "HW_DESC=MO1008-0000,SLAVE_ID=7" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "HW_DESC=MO2008-0000,SLAVE_ID=8" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "HW_DESC=MO2338-0000,SLAVE_ID=9" Each descriptor also accepts either suffix, for example HW_DESC=MO2008-0000-1112. These explicit variants reuse the generic ecmcMO1008-0000.substitutions, ecmcMO2008-0000.substitutions or ecmcMO2338-0000-common.substitutions database, respectively.
Enable a second baseplate with EtherLab Issue EtherLab discovers only the first MX baseplate, while TwinCAT can activate the downstream baseplate. The downstream MS4210 is not visible in EtherLab at all, so neither it nor the EtherCAT modules connected through it appear in the slave list. The MS4210 is normally installed in the last slot of the upstream baseplate.
Root cause The internal MB1120 backplane junction, for this baseplate at slave position 10, starts with EtherCAT port 3 forced Closed.
The relevant EtherCAT Slave Controller (ESC) register is:
 0x0100: DL Control MB1120 default: 0x0007c001 Port 3 set to Auto: 0x00070001  Observed topology and slave positions  The MB1120 is the backplane-junction EtherCAT slave that controls access to the next downstream baseplate. Its slave position is the value passed as MB1120_SID, or as MX_1 through MX_5 during startup. For multiple baseplates, specify the MB1120 positions in upstream-to-downstream discovery order. The MB1100-002 Bluetooth gateway seems to offset subsequent EtherCAT slave positions by one. Account for this when determining the MB1120 slave position used by the workaround. The MS1110-0000 always seems to appear as the last slave. With one baseplate it is last in that topology; when a second baseplate is enabled, it moves to the end of the expanded topology.  Workaround Set port 3 to Auto, wait for the downstream baseplate to become available, and list the slaves again:
ethercat reg_write -m1 -p10 -e -t uint32 0x0100 0x00070001 sleep 1 ethercat slaves -m1 Adjust the master (-m1) and slave position (-p10) to match the system.
The same operation is available as an ecmccfg script. The MB1120 slave position defaults to 10, and the master defaults to ECMC_EC_MASTER_ID (or 0 if it is not set). The script uses the ECMC_EC_TOOL_PATH configured by startup.cmd:
mxEnableDownStreamBaseplate.cmd can only be used before addMaster.cmd claims the EtherCAT master. For normal IOC startup, use the MX_1 through MX_5 startup macros described below.
 ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}mxEnableDownStreamBaseplate.cmd Override the defaults with script macros when required:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}mxEnableDownStreamBaseplate.cmd, "MASTER_ID=1,MB1120_SID=10" Set REPORT=1 to list the EtherCAT slaves before and after enabling the downstream baseplate. Reporting is disabled by default. Before rescanning, the script waits three seconds by default; override this with RESCAN_DELAY:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}mxEnableDownStreamBaseplate.cmd, "REPORT=1,RESCAN_DELAY=3" The junctions must be opened before ecmc claims the EtherCAT master. For IOC startup, set MX_1 through MX_5 to the MB1120 slave positions. The populated macros are processed in order, with a rescan after each junction so the next downstream MB1120 becomes visible:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}startup.cmd, "SYS=...,MX_1=10,MX_2=21,MX_REPORT=1" Omit unused MX_n macros. MX_REPORT defaults to 0, and MX_RESCAN_DELAY defaults to 3 seconds.
MO2338-0000-1112 M12 pinout and BO02 LED indication Each M12 A-coded connector carries two digital input/output channels:
   Pin Signal     1 +24 V (UB)   2 DIO B   3 GND   4 DIO A   5 Not connected    The channels are assigned in A/B pairs. On the first connector, BO01 is DIO A on pin 4 and BO02 is DIO B on pin 2. The following connectors carry BO03/BO04, BO05/BO06, and BO07/BO08 in the same pattern.
On one MO2338-0000-1112, the BO02 LED was observed to remain off while all of the following showed that the output was operating correctly:
 BO-Arr-RB returned 0xff after writing 0xff to BO-Arr. Pin 2 of the first M12 connector measured 24 V. BO-Stat01, BO-Stat02, and BO-Stat03 were all zero. EFU-Stat was 0x4008, indicating that the electronic fuse was enabled without a warning, error, or trip.  Do not use the BO02 LED alone to determine the electrical output state. Verify BO-Arr-RB, the BO diagnostics, and the voltage between pin 2 and pin 3.
Restoring missing SII data: MO1008 example One MO1008-0000-1112 was found with an incomplete or corrupt SII EEPROM. The terminal identity could still be read, but its descriptive and process-data information was absent. In this condition, ethercat slaves showed only the numeric vendor ID and product code instead of the terminal name:
8 0:8 PREOP + 0x00000002:0x811fbc0b ethercat pdos returned no PDOs. Likewise, ethercat xml contained only the numeric identity and no SyncManager or PDO definitions. An ethercat sii_read -v returned only a minimal 128-byte SII area.
When ecmc configured an input PDO on SM3, EtherLab consequently reported:
EtherCAT ERROR 1-8: Failed to determine PDO sync manager for FMMU! This error occurs before, and independently of, packing the 0x1a00 input PDO as U8 or the 0x1a01 diagnosis PDO as U16. EtherLab creates the FMMU from the application configuration, but cannot resolve SM3 because the physical SyncManager descriptions are missing from the slave’s SII. Adding an ecmc Cfg.EcAddSyncManager() call does not restore those SII descriptions.
The matching ESI specifies the relevant process-data SyncManagers as:
   SyncManager Start address Size Control byte Direction     SM2 0x1200 2 bytes 0x24 Outputs   SM3 0x1900 11 bytes 0x20 Inputs    The terminal needs a valid binary SII EEPROM image generated from the matching ESI or read from an identical working MO1008-0000-1112. Back up the existing EEPROM before writing anything. The XML ESI file cannot be passed directly to ethercat sii_write; that command expects a compiled binary SII image.
Write the matching binary SII image SII means Slave Information Interface (not SSI). The following field example restored the device name of an MO1008-0000-1112 on master 1, slave position 7. The earlier diagnostic example used position 8; always select the position from the current bus listing.
Carry out EEPROM maintenance with the machine stopped and motion disabled. Confirm the physical module, variant, revision, master ID and slave position before writing. Use a binary SII image matching that hardware; do not copy an image from a different module or bypass image checks with --force.
   Inspect the target and save its existing SII contents, even if incomplete:
ethercat -m1 slaves ethercat -m1 -p7 slaves -v ethercat -m1 -p7 sii_read > MO1008-0000-1112-m1-p7-before.bin Check that the read succeeded before proceeding. Omit -v from sii_read when saving a binary backup; verbose output is text.
Before the repair, the relevant line was:
7 0:7 PREOP + 0x00000002:0x811fbc0b   Write the matching binary image. In this installation it was stored at:
ethercat -m1 -p7 sii_write /ioc/NeedfulThings/beckhoff_firmwares/p05_sii_MO1008-0000-1112.bin Replace the path with the location of your verified image. The p05 in this filename does not select the destination: -m1 -p7 selects master 1, slave position 7. Use the permissions required by the local EtherCAT setup.
  Rescan the selected master to refresh its cached slave information:
ethercat -m1 rescan ethercat -m1 slaves In the reported sequence, ethercat slaves immediately after sii_write still showed the numeric identity. After the rescan it showed:
7 0:7 PREOP + MO1008-0000-1112 8-channel digital input, 24 V DC, M12 The rescan rereads slave information; an unchanged name before rescan does not by itself mean the write failed. Do not repeat the write just to refresh the displayed name.
  Check the restored PDO and SyncManager descriptions:
ethercat -m1 -p7 sii_read -v ethercat -m1 -p7 pdos ethercat -m1 -p7 xml Confirm that the expected descriptions are present, then validate the ecmc configuration, slave state and input data on the hardware.
  The observed rescan restored the MO1008 name, but did not establish that the whole bus was healthy. Other positions still showed INIT E, and positions 10 and 11 showed zero identities or an unknown state in the subsequent listing. Check every expected slave after rescanning and resolve those issues before returning the machine to operation. Restoring the name alone does not validate PDO operation or prove that all SII data are correct.
The generic MO1008-0000 and MO1008-0000-1112 ecmccfg mappings use the matching Beckhoff ESI’s default Synchron mode (AssignActivate=0x100): RX 0x1680 (EFU control) on SM2, and TX 0x1a00 (inputs), 0x1a01 (input diagnosis), and 0x1a80 (EFU status/current) on SM3. Earlier configurations omitted the required RX PDO and incorrectly assigned EFU inputs to 0x1a10. Use the corrected configuration after restoring SII. The reported SII write and rescan confirm device-name recovery; process-data validation remains a separate commissioning step.
MS1010-1002-1334 rail shutdown and recovery Setting bit 0 (Disable Output) in PSU-Ctrl removes power from the complete 24 V rail. Despite sometimes being described operationally as an enable control, this bit is active-high disable and must not be toggled casually.
On the tested MS1010-1002-1334, clearing the bit did not immediately restore the rail. The slave had to be power-cycled and remain fully unpowered for at least 30 seconds before it would feed power again. Account for the loss of all devices supplied by that rail before operating this control.
 Automatic downstream-baseplate discovery utility The utils/mxEnableDownstreamBaseplates.sh utility can discover and open a chain without specifying the MB1120 positions in advance. It repeatedly finds the last newly visible MB1120, opens port 3, waits, and rescans until no new MB1120 is found:
utils/mxEnableDownstreamBaseplates.sh 1 3 /opt/etherlab/bin/ethercat 3 The positional arguments are the master ID (default 0) and rescan delay in seconds (default 3), followed by the optional EtherCAT executable (default /opt/etherlab/bin/ethercat) and EtherCAT port (default 3). Ports 0 through 3 are accepted. MX_MAX_BASEPLATES sets the safety limit and defaults to 32.
Run this utility before addMaster.cmd claims the EtherCAT master.
 Related Pages  hardware ethercat command line interface FSoE and TwinSAFE

title: ecmc_cfg_tool
content:
ecmc_cfg_tool is an external runtime tool repository for interacting with ecmc through the ecmc command parser. It is useful when you need to inspect and adjust settings on a running system.
What It Is Good For  Reading status and configuration values from a running ecmc instance. Adjusting axis/drive/encoder related settings at runtime. Testing command-parser based changes before writing them into static startup/YAML configuration.  Controller Tuning App ecmc_cfg_tool includes a dedicated controller configurator app (start_cntrl.sh/ecmc_cntrl_qt.py). It builds and uses a controller-focused command catalog and provides runtime read/write access to:
 PID core parameters (Kp, Ki, Kd, Kff) Inner-loop PID parameters and tolerance Deadband and deadband time Output and integral limits At-target monitor parameters Scaling numerator/denominator  Motion App (mtn) The motion app (start_mtn.sh/ecmc_mtn_qt.py) is a motor-record based runtime motion test UI. It provides:
 Absolute/relative moves and jog control (forward/backward) A<->B sequence test with step count, idle time, and snake mode Drive enable/disable plus explicit STOP/KILL actions Compact runtime trend plots for position/setpoint/error  Axis Config App (axis) The axis app (start_axis.sh/ecmc_axis_cfg.py) is a YAML-oriented runtime configuration UI. It loads an axis YAML template and maps keys to command-parser Get/Set commands for:
 Per-parameter read/write operations Bulk Read All, Copy Read->Set, and Write Filled Session change tracking and “Changed YAML” export view Optional YAML-to-command mapping overrides via *.command_map.csv  Stream App (stream) The stream app (start.sh/ecmc_stream_qt.py) is the generic command-parser frontend. It provides:
 Direct CMD/QRY access for arbitrary ecmc command parser calls Catalog-based command browser with descriptions and runtime metadata Blocklist support to mark/hide blocked commands Multi-command editor panels for grouped command workflows  How It Fits With ecmccfg ecmc_cfg_tool complements ecmccfg by operating at runtime. It does not replace static configuration files or IOC startup scripts.
Typical flow:
 Start the IOC and load your normal configuration with ecmccfg/loadYamlAxis.cmd. Use ecmc_cfg_tool to inspect and adjust settings through the ecmc command parser. Persist useful runtime changes back into your YAML/startup configuration as needed.  Runtime Still Uses loadYamlAxis.cmd Initial axis configuration is still typically loaded through:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}loadYamlAxis.cmd, "FILE=./cfg/ax1.yaml, DEV=${DEV}, DRV_SLAVE=4, ENC_SLAVE=3, ENC_CHANNEL=01" Notes  Treat ecmc_cfg_tool runtime changes as temporary until reflected in versioned config files. At PSI, the tool can also be started from the generic ecmcMain.ui panel. Follow the ecmc_cfg_tool repository README for exact install/CLI usage, as that tool can evolve independently of ecmccfg.

title: Motor position and soft-limit autosave
content:
Scope and required support Motor position restoration and soft-limit restoration are separate features. This page describes the ECMC motor-record startup restore implementation and its startup gate. Use an ECMC build containing that implementation; adding an option to YAML does not add support to an older binary.
For the complete incremental stepper setup, see the stepper_openloop_asr example.
Enable soft-limit restoration in YAML epics: name: Axis1 motorRecord: restoreSoftLimits: true syncSoftLimits: true # false keeps the restored pair motor-local restoreSoftLimits is a startup-only policy. syncSoftLimits remains runtime-configurable. With restore enabled and sync disabled, autosave-restored motor limits remain local and enabled ECMC limits bound them without being modified. With both enabled, the restored pair is copied to ECMC and ongoing synchronization is enabled.
For backward compatibility, advanced configurations may still put restoreMotorSoftLims=1 in axis.parameters; mode 1 restores into ECMC and forces synchronization. Internal mode 2 performs motor-local restoration. Normal YAML configurations should use the two booleans above rather than these numeric driver modes.
Without the restore option, ECMC seeds the motor’s limits from its configured limits at startup. Saving the motor limit fields alone does not make restored values authoritative in that mode.
After changing soft limits, reload any open caQtDM panels. Numeric input widgets, such as the motor VAL field, use the limits read when the panel was opened and can reject values based on the previous limits until the panel is reloaded.
Three soft-limit arrangements ECMC supports three useful arrangements. They differ in which layer enforces a limit and whether changes propagate between the motor record and ECMC. The complete PSI IOC projects are under examples/PSI/lab_setup/asr. They deliberately share the MTEST04-EC-ASR IOC identity and the same hardware; install and run only one project at a time.
   Arrangement Motor limits ECMC limits Runtime synchronization     Motor only Autosave-restored Disabled Off   Motor and ECMC, independent Autosave-restored and bounded by ECMC YAML-configured Off   Motor and ECMC, synchronized Autosave-restored Replaced by the restored motor pair On    All three arrangements save only the motor dial fields:
MTEST04-EC-ASR:M1.DLLM MTEST04-EC-ASR:M1.DHLM Do not add -CfgDLLM, -CfgDHLM, their readbacks, or their enable records to the same autosave request. Those records create a second, competing restore path.
Motor limits only Use motor-only limits when motor-record commands should be constrained but ECMC native commands may bypass that range. Disable ECMC limits and enable motor-local restoration without synchronization:
epics: name: M1 motorRecord: restoreSoftLimits: true syncSoftLimits: false fieldInit: 'DLLM=-50,DHLM=50,RTRY=0,FOFF=Frozen' softlimits: enable: false fieldInit supplies the motor defaults used when no save file exists. Autosave overwrites .DLLM/.DHLM when a saved pair is available. Because ECMC limits are disabled, native commands are not protected by these motor-only limits. See softlimits_motor_only.
Independent motor and ECMC limits Use independent limits when ECMC must enforce an outer safety envelope while the motor record uses a narrower operator range:
epics: name: M1 motorRecord: restoreSoftLimits: true syncSoftLimits: false softlimits: enable: true backward: -100 backwardEnable: true forward: 100 forwardEnable: true For example, autosave may restore motor limits -80, 80 while ECMC remains at -100, 100. With synchronization off, later motor edits do not change ECMC. The enabled ECMC limits are nevertheless the maximum range accepted by the motor record, so restored motor limits must lie inside the ECMC envelope. See softlimits_motor_and_ecmc.
After restart, the expected values for that example are:
M1.DLLM/M1.DHLM -80 / 80 M1-CfgDLLM-RB/M1-CfgDHLM-RB -100 / 100 M1-CfgSyncSftLim No Synchronized motor and ECMC limits Use synchronized limits when both interfaces should expose and enforce the same restored pair:
epics: name: M1 motorRecord: restoreSoftLimits: true syncSoftLimits: true softlimits: enable: true backward: -100 backwardEnable: true forward: 100 forwardEnable: true At startup, the autosave-restored motor pair replaces the YAML ECMC pair. Later motor-limit edits propagate to ECMC, and ECMC limit changes propagate back to the motor record. See softlimits_motor_and_ecmc_synced.
Which values are used? The standard YAML generator initializes the motor record’s .DLLM and .DHLM from the YAML soft-limit configuration. Autosave can overwrite those fields while the IOC initializes. ECMC then snapshots the initialized motor fields and applies the selected motor-local or synchronized restore policy.
   Configuration Startup source of the restored limit pair     Restore option, with autosave restoring .DLLM and .DHLM Autosave-restored motor fields   Restore option, with no autosave restore of those fields Motor fields initialized by the standard YAML generator   No restore option Configured ECMC limits seed the motor at startup    The driver does not detect whether autosave supplied a field. It uses the motor record values after initialization. Without a saved pair, the standard generated motor record retains its YAML- or fieldInit-derived values. In synchronized mode, a saved pair replaces the configured ECMC pair. In independent mode, the saved motor pair remains local and must fit inside the enabled ECMC envelope. A custom motor template must initialize its dial fields consistently with the desired arrangement.
Autosave request and restore passes For an IOC named MTEST04-MTN-ASM, use cfg/MTEST04-MTN-ASM_pos.req:
# Position restoration is controlled separately by the motor's RSTM field. MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DVAL # Soft limits are dial coordinates, in engineering units. MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DLLM MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DHLM Do not also restore the writable -CfgDLLM and -CfgDHLM records for the same axis. That creates competing restore paths. Do not save -RB readback records as configuration. Configure the ECMC limit values and enable flags in YAML for the independent arrangement.
With the PSI ioc install workflow, a filename ending in _pos.req selects the two-pass restore setup. For a differently named request, the PSI directive #ENABLE-PASS=2 requests that setup. Verify that the generated restore script contains both actual autosave pass registrations before iocInit:
set_pass0_restoreFile "MTEST04-MTN-ASM_pos.sav" set_pass1_restoreFile "MTEST04-MTN-ASM_pos.sav" Autosave calls these passes 0 and 1; the PSI directive’s value 2 denotes the two-pass setup. A .req lists fields to save. The .sav contains the values which will actually be restored, so inspect it when troubleshooting.
Position restoration and MRES The restore option above concerns soft limits only. Position uses the saved .DVAL and the motor’s RSTM policy. In the ESS motor implementation, the NearZero default restores a nonzero saved position when the initial readback is near zero, according to the motor deadband. It does not request restoration of a saved zero. Always is a different, explicit position-restoration policy; do not change it merely to troubleshoot soft limits.
This example uses an incremental encoder (encoder.type: 0), whose counter position can be restored through the motor. Soft-limit restoration can be used independently of position restoration.
ECMC uses engineering units. An ECMC-specific motor template should establish MF_DRIVER_USES_EGU from database loading, for example:
field(MFLG, "$(MFLG=8)") Mask 8 (1 << 3) selects the driver’s engineering-unit convention. It does not select a position-restore policy or request zeroing. Keep the real MRES scaling; do not set MRES to 1 to conceal a limit conversion problem. The ECMC compatibility init hook also sets the EGU flag before motor-record initialization.
Startup sequence, step by step With restoreSoftLimits: true and ECMC_STARTUP_GATE=1, startup proceeds as follows:
 Load the YAML configuration, before iocInit. ECMC receives the configured soft limits. The standard motor template also initializes .DLLM and .DHLM from those limits, for example -100 and 100. Hold limit readback while restoration is pending. The driver suppresses ECMC-to-motor soft-limit updates so that the configured limits cannot overwrite values restored into the motor record. Autosave restores the motor fields during iocInit. Restore passes 0 and 1 load .DLLM and .DHLM, for example -123 and 123. .DVAL is restored separately and follows the motor’s position-restoration policy. Capture the restored limits after the IOC is running. At initHookAfterIocRunning, ECMC captures the motor record’s .DLLM, .DHLM and .MRES. This is an IOC initialization hook, not an autosave callback. If autosave did not replace the fields, their template defaults are captured. Allow native axis initialization. Once the IOC is running and bus/timing health has been good continuously for two seconds, the gate allows native axis initialization. Drives, motion commands and ordinary cyclic command producers remain held. Complete the selected restore policy. With synchronization enabled, the motor poller applies the captured pair to ECMC under the RT mutex; failed attempts are retried. With synchronization disabled, the captured pair stays in the motor record and ECMC either retains its YAML envelope or remains disabled in the motor-only arrangement. Deliver the first healthy motor status. The compatibility workaround handles a stale startup COMM_ALARM once, under the motor-record lock, before normal asyn status delivery. This permits a deferred position-load command to proceed. Complete position restoration, if requested by RSTM. The motor sends the saved .DVAL through asyn to ECMC. Startup waits for motor-record completion and a subsequent RT sample acknowledging the loaded coordinate; merely queueing the command is not sufficient. Release the remaining startup gate. Every native axis must finish initialization, and every loaded motor record must complete its startup handshake. Ordinary PLCs, plugins and other motion command producers can then run, and a configured startup enable can be applied. An axis without a loaded motor record does not wait for a motor-record handshake. Continue normal operation. Synchronized mode propagates changes in both directions. Independent and motor-only modes keep motor edits local. Autosave saves the motor dial fields for the next restart.  Complete startup before motion Set the gate explicitly before ecmccfg enters runtime:
epicsEnvSet("ECMC_STARTUP_GATE", "1") With the gate enabled, native axis initialization proceeds with drives disabled. Ordinary PLC/plugin cyclic execution, motion sequences, PVT, master/slave state machines, C++ logic and position compare remain held until every native axis and every loaded motor record has completed startup. This includes restored limits, the position-load handshake when requested, and a subsequent RT sample acknowledging the loaded coordinate. Axes without a loaded motor record do not wait for one. Early motion/enable requests are rejected, not replayed later; STOP, disable, coordinate loading and status polling remain available.
Configuration and plugin/logic enter-RT initialization hooks still run to prepare runtime; supported motion/enable commands from those hooks are held too. The dedicated safety plugin and bus/disabled-axis I/O continue operating. Gate 0 selects legacy startup and does not provide this guarantee. START_EPICS_FIRST changes startup order; its fixed delay is not a substitute for the gate.
The ECMC motor-record compatibility workaround clears only a stale startup COMM_ALARM, once a healthy sample and live axis state have been verified. It uses EPICS alarm handling under the record lock before delivering the asyn callback, allowing a deferred position load to be queued. It preserves other alarms and does not repeatedly clear runtime communication faults. This is a narrow exception to normal motor-record alarm ownership; it does not change motorECMC or bypass asyn command delivery.
See startup configuration for startup ordering. Verify a known nonzero saved position and limits different from YAML defaults before the log announcing release of PLCs and motion command producers. Repeat with no loaded motor record and with a stalled restore or bus fault; incomplete startup must leave motion held.

title: Native target-write motion
content:
Native axes normally stage a target position and wait for an EXECUTE request. The optional target-write mode starts an ABS or REL move when the target is written. It is configured separately for each axis and is disabled by default.
The axis can move without EXECUTE when this mode is enabled.
Writing the native target-position PV starts motion, similar to writing .VAL on an EPICS motor record. Editing the target in a panel, writing it from a script, or restoring it from a saved value is therefore a motion request—not just preparation for a later execute command. Each accepted write triggers, including an identical REL value written again. Configured auto-enable can enable a disabled drive and start the move.
 Enable, query and disable For axis 6, use these ECMC command strings:
Cfg.SetAxisAutoExec(6,1) GetAxisAutoExec(6) Cfg.SetAxisAutoExec(6,0) The query returns 1 for target-write mode and 0 for the default staged mode. In an IOC startup script, opt in after creating and configuring the axis:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisAutoExec(6,1)" Selecting the mode does not execute an already staged target. Disabling the mode restores separate target/execute handling; it does not stop an active move. Use the normal native STOP command or -StpCmd PV to stop motion.
The longer names SetAxisAutoExecuteOnTargetPos and GetAxisAutoExecuteOnTargetPos remain accepted aliases. Prefer the short names over MCU-Cmd.AOUT, which has a 39-character usable string limit even when the asyn record’s OMAX is larger.
Motion behavior Configure the motion command, velocity, acceleration and deceleration before writing a target. The supported command types are:
   Native command Meaning of the written target     3: ABS Absolute target position   2: REL Relative distance using the existing relative-move semantics    These native interfaces trigger motion in this mode:
 The axis -TgtPosCmd PV, linked to ax6.targpos for axis 6. The text command Main.M6.fPosition=<value>. The C API setAxisTargetPos(6,value).  A write during an active position move of the same type retargets that move. Requests during another motion type or pending enable/start preparation are rejected rather than queued. Homing and velocity commands require their normal trigger interfaces.
Motor-record .VAL behavior and internal PLC/sequencer setpoint updates are unchanged. Enabling target-write mode does not turn a continuously updated PLC setpoint into a new move every RT cycle.
Auto-enable and interlocks The existing axis auto-enable sequence is supported. For example:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisAutoEnableTimeout(6,5)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEnableAutoEnable(6,1)" Motion waits for the normal drive enable acknowledgement and coordinated start permission. With auto-enable disabled, a disabled axis rejects a target-triggered move. The normal startup holds, command ownership, trajectory-source checks, axis errors, limits and interlocks still apply.
Panel indication and readback <axis-prefix>-AutoExecuteOnTargetPos-RB reports the selected mode. For example, SIMSLIT:TR_HI-AutoExecuteOnTargetPos-RB belongs to the TR_HI axis in that IOC. It is a read-only indicator; use the configuration command to change the mode.
The main and native axis panels show a compact amber NO EXEC badge when the mode is enabled. The expert panel shows NO EXEC needed. Hover over the badge for the explanation that target writes start motion. The badge is hidden in the default mode, where EXECUTE remains required.
The mode is status-word bit 24. Sequence state and last interlock now occupy the low and next byte of axN.status2; its upper 16 bits are reserved. Install matching ECMC and ecmccfg versions when adopting this status layout. Existing -SeqState and -LastIlock PV names use the updated decoding.
For the existing motor-record interface, see Motor Record.

title: PVT
content:
Scope This page describes profile-move / PVT motion in ecmccfg.
Here, PVT means the asyn motor-controller profile-move workflow where:
 each participating axis provides a position array the controller provides the common timing array the profile is built, executed, and optionally read back after motion  When To Use PVT Use PVT when a single move should follow a precomputed trajectory instead of one target point at a time.
Typical cases:
 scanning along a fixed point sequence synchronized multi-axis trajectories trajectories that must be prepared and checked before execution  Configuration Overview PVT has two parts:
 axis-side enablement in the YAML axis config controller-side PVT records created by pvtControllerConfig.cmd  Axis YAML PVT is enabled per axis in the motor-record block:
epics: name: Axis1 precision: 3 motorRecord: enable: true pvt: npoints: 20 nreadback: 20 Meaning:
 epics.motorRecord.pvt.npoints: max number of target points for this axis epics.motorRecord.pvt.nreadback: max number of readback points for this axis  When this block is present, the axis loader:
 loads axis-specific PVT PVs like Axis1-PVT-UseAxis and Axis1-PVT-Positions enables PVT for the axis in the motor driver stores the maximum sizes needed by the controller-level PVT records  Startup Sequence Minimal pattern:
require ecmccfg "ENG_MODE=1,MASTER_ID=0" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "SLAVE_ID=14,HW_DESC=EL7041-0052" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Generic-2Phase-Stepper,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=1000,I_STDBY_MA=500,U_NOM_MV=48000,R_COIL_MOHM=1230,STEPS=400'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}loadYamlAxis.cmd, "FILE=./cfg/axis.yaml,DEV=${IOC},DRV_SLAVE=${ECMC_EC_SLAVE_NUM}" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}pvtControllerConfig.cmd This pattern is used in:
 examples/PSI/best_practice/motion/pvt/el7041_0052/  pvtControllerConfig.cmd pvtControllerConfig.cmd creates the shared controller-side PVT records and allocates the profile buffers in the asyn motor driver.
Important macros:
 NPOINTS: max number of profile points NREADBACK: max number of readback points NPULSES: max number of output pulses NAXES: number of participating axes TRG_EC_ENTRY: optional EtherCAT entry linked to the PVT trigger output TRG_DUR_S: optional pulse duration for the trigger output SOFT_TRG_FLNK: optional forward link from PVT-SftTrg  If these sizes are not supplied explicitly, the script uses the largest values collected from all axes with epics.motorRecord.pvt.
Automatic versus explicit configuration If PVT is enabled for one or more axes and pvtControllerConfig.cmd was not called manually, setAppMode.cmd will run a default pvtControllerConfig.cmd automatically.
Call pvtControllerConfig.cmd explicitly when you need to:
 configure trigger output with TRG_EC_ENTRY override sizes manually configure the controller before setAppMode.cmd  Direct motor-record iocsh commands For normal ecmccfg usage, the YAML loader and pvtControllerConfig.cmd handle the required motor-record setup for you.
The underlying motor-record layer in ecmc also exposes direct iocsh commands:
ecmcCreateProfile(<controllerPort>, <maxPoints>) ecmcEnablePVTForAxis(<controllerPort>, <axisId>, <enable>) Use these only when working directly with the low-level motor-record controller layer rather than the normal ecmccfg startup flow.
Meaning:
 ecmcCreateProfile(...) allocates the shared profile buffer for the selected controller ecmcEnablePVTForAxis(...) enables or disables PVT support for one axis on that controller  In a normal ecmccfg IOC:
 pvtControllerConfig.cmd covers the controller-side allocation YAML epics.motorRecord.pvt covers per-axis enablement  Main PVs Controller-level PVs These PVs are created from ecmcProfileMoveController.template with prefix $(P)PVT-....
Important PVs:
 PVT-NumAxes: number of axes used in the profile PVT-NumPoints: number of profile points PVT-NumPulses: number of output pulses PVT-StartPulses: point index where trigger pulses start PVT-EndPulses: point index where trigger pulses stop PVT-TimeMode: fixed time or array time mode PVT-FixedTime: fixed time per point PVT-Times: time array PVT-MoveMode: absolute or relative move PVT-Build: build/check the profile PVT-BuildState, PVT-BuildStatus, PVT-BuildMessage: build diagnostics PVT-Execute: execute the built profile PVT-ExecuteState, PVT-ExecuteStatus, PVT-ExecuteMessage: execution diagnostics PVT-Abort: abort profile execution PVT-Readback: request profile readback arrays PVT-ReadbackState, PVT-ReadbackStatus, PVT-ReadbackMessage: readback diagnostics PVT-SftTrg: software trigger helper record  Axis-level PVs These PVs are created for each PVT-enabled axis from ecmcProfileMoveAxis.template.
Important PVs:
 <Axis>-PVT-UseAxis: include this axis in the profile <Axis>-PVT-Positions: target positions for this axis <Axis>-PVT-Readbacks: actual readback positions after readback <Axis>-PVT-FollowingErrors: following-error array after readback  Minimal Workflow Typical sequence from EPICS:
 Set PVT-NumPoints Set PVT-NumPulses and optionally PVT-StartPulses / PVT-EndPulses Select PVT-TimeMode If using array timing, write PVT-Times For each participating axis, set <Axis>-PVT-UseAxis=1 Write <Axis>-PVT-Positions Set PVT-Build=1 and verify PVT-BuildStatus Set PVT-Execute=1 Optionally set PVT-Readback=1 and inspect <Axis>-PVT-Readbacks  Example:
caput IOC:PVT-NumPoints 7 caput IOC:PVT-NumPulses 5 caput IOC:PVT-MoveMode 0 caput IOC:Axis1-PVT-UseAxis 1 caput -a IOC:Axis1-PVT-Positions "0 360 720 1080 1440 1080 720" caput -a IOC:PVT-Times "1 2 2 1 5 1 1" caput IOC:PVT-Build 1 caput IOC:PVT-Execute 1 Notes:
 PVT-MoveMode=0 means absolute mode. In fixed-time mode, PVT-FixedTime is used instead of the PVT-Times array. Build and execute are separate steps.  Trigger Output If TRG_EC_ENTRY is configured in pvtControllerConfig.cmd, the PVT controller can drive an EtherCAT output during the profile.
Use this when the motion profile must emit synchronized trigger pulses to external hardware.
Relevant settings:
 TRG_EC_ENTRY: output bit or entry to link to the PVT trigger object TRG_DUR_S: trigger pulse duration PVT-StartPulses, PVT-EndPulses, PVT-NumPulses: pulse placement/count  Current Documentation Gaps PVT support exists in the codebase and templates, but it is still only lightly covered elsewhere in the manual.
The axis YAML keys epics.motorRecord.pvt.npoints and epics.motorRecord.pvt.nreadback are documented in the YAML reference and should be considered required for YAML-based PVT setup.
The preferred example to start from is:
 examples/PSI/best_practice/motion/pvt/el7041_0052/  Related Pages  Motor Record Axis YAML Script Reference

title: Technosoft iPOS4808, iPOS8020
content:
Scope Use this page for Technosoft iPOS drive setup, especially FoE-based base configuration and the PSI-supported starter configurations.
iPOSXXXX Main use cases for Technosoft drives at PSI are applications requiring:
 high currents STO (Safe Torque Off) DC motors  Configuration Technosoft drives are powerful, but they are not especially simple to integrate. Many settings are not exposed as normal CoE SDOs, so a base configuration needs to be created in one of the Technosoft tools and downloaded before the drive is used for the first time. That step is normally only needed once. These base configurations contain most of the setup, and only smaller adjustments can later be made over SDOs from the EtherCAT master.
These configurations can be transferred in several ways:
 RS232: Technosoft Easy Motion Studio 1, EasySetup RS232: Technosoft Easy Motion Studio 2 CoE: CAN bus over EtherCAT, mailbox protocol (by writing to generic memory interface addresses; not intuitive) FoE: File over EtherCAT, mailbox protocol (Easy Motion Studio 2 -> Export -> FoE -> Complete Config)  To avoid downloading a configuration to each drive over local RS232, a few generic configurations have been developed and exported via FoE and/or CoE:
 Open-loop stepper, 48V, STO (no support for encoders). Encoders need to be connected to other EtherCAT slaves like EL5042 or EL5102.   Max current, standby current, and current-control parameters can be set over SDO.  Pure voltage control for brushed DC motors  These configuration files can be found in ecmccfg/hardware/Technosoft_slaves/config/.
These configurations are intentionally basic and do not expose all hardware features supported by the drive. For example, the following is not covered:
 encoders, which need dedicated configuration files for each BiSS bit count and cannot realistically be configured only over SDOs …  Download config over FoE (File over EtherCAT) NOTE: The configuration normally only needs to be downloaded once, before the first use of the drive.
Requirements from Technosoft CoE manual (https://technosoftmotion.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/P091.064.EtherCAT.iPOS_.UM.pdf):
 Find an appropriate configuration in ecmccfg/hardware/Technosoft_slaves/config/ The FoE file must start with “FOESW_”. The entire FoE file name length must not exceed 14 characters (including extension). A setup data file can be transferred via FoE protocol only in BOOT (manual states differently, but mailbox size in OP and PREOP is wrong). The password to program a FoE setup data file is 0 and appears not to be used in practice.  Configure drive (download file, write file)  Identify the correct binary configuration file in ecmccfg/hardware/Technosoft_slaves/config/. Allow writes in BOOT by writing 1 to 0x210c 0x0: ethercat download -m<masterid> -p<slaveid> 0x210c 0x0 1 Set drive EtherCAT state to BOOT (even though the manual states download should be made in PREOP, OP or SAFEOP): ethercat states -m<masterid> -p<slaveid> BOOT Download file: ethercat -m<masterid> -p<slaveid> foe_write <filename> Power-cycle the drive so the new configuration is loaded.  Example Example:
 Master id: 0 Slave id: 21 Config file (binary): “FOESW_OL48.bin”  # 2. Allow FoE in state BOOT ethercat download -m0 -p21 0x210c 0x0 1 # 3a. Set slave into state BOOT ethercat states -m0 -p21 BOOT # 3b. Check that slave is in boot state ethercat slaves # 4. Download configuration file ethercat foe_write -m0 -p21 FOESW_OL48.bin # 5. Now power cycle drive Upload file (read file) NOTE 1: Normally upload of the configuration is not needed!
 You must know the name of the file on the slave ethercat -m<masterid> -p<slaveid> foe_read <filename> > <output filename>  Note: -o or --output-file does not appear to work here.
Example ethercat -m0 -p0 foe_read FOESW_8020.bin > test.bin Generate new config file in EasyMotion Studio 1  Create the configuration in EasyMotion Studio. Select Application -> Create EtherCAT FOE File -> Setup Only. Choose filename and save (note: max 14 chars). Store the file in ecmccfg/hardware/Technosoft_slaves/config/FoE/<suitable_dir_name>/<suitable_file_name> Add a README.md file in ecmccfg/hardware/Technosoft_slaves/config/FoE/<suitable_dir_name>/ describing the config:   Drive type (8020BX-CAT or 4808BX-CAT) DC-link voltage (48V) Control mode (normally always CSV) …  ECMC Example Configuration for iPOS4808 require ecmccfg "ENG_MODE=1" #- Note the "_2" in iPOS4808BX_2 ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "SLAVE_ID=21, HW_DESC=iPOS4808BX_2" epicsEnvSet("ECMC_EC_SLAVE_NUM_DRIVE", "$(ECMC_EC_SLAVE_NUM)") #- NOTE USE HW_DESC = iPOS4808BX_2 (iPOS4808BX is for legacy) #- Apply component: Oriental motor PKE244A #- For IPOS4808 some macros are mandatory: #- * I_CTRL_GAIN : Current loop gain #- * I_CTRL_INT : Current loop integrator gain #- * I_MAX_MA : Mandatory if Motor-Generic-2Phase-Stepper is used #- * I_STDBY_MA : Mandatory if Motor-Generic-2Phase-Stepper is used #- The values can be taken from EasyMotionStudio or by trial and error (coil resistance and inductance are not used in the iPOS cfgs) #- After running a tuning test in EasyMotionStudio, a reset is needed (from Easy Motion Studio or over SDO; see motor cfg scripts). ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Generic-2Phase-Stepper, MACROS='I_MAX_MA=1000,I_STDBY_MA=100,CURR_KP=1.0,CURR_TI=0.26'" #- ############################################################################# #- AXIS 1 #- The reduced current will be applied automatically by the iPOS4808 (no links needed in axis cfgs) #- $(SCRIPTEXEC) ($(ecmccfg_DIR)configureAxis.cmd, CONFIG=./cfg/ipos4808_1.ax) ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}loadYamlAxis.cmd, "FILE=./cfg/axis.yaml, DEV=${IOC}, AX_NAME=M1, AXIS_ID=1, DRV_SID=${ECMC_EC_SLAVE_NUM}" Related Pages  hardware motion configuration

title: ecmccomp
content:
ecmccomp is the component library for ecmc. It provides reusable component definitions (motors, encoders, and slave-specific configs) that are applied to EtherCAT slaves at IOC startup.
What it is for  Reusing validated motor, encoder, and slave configuration blocks across installations Keeping component parameters in engineering units and converting them to slave-specific SDO values Applying configuration consistently with built-in compatibility and macro validation  Main entry point: applyComponent.cmd The standard entry script is:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccomp_DIR}applyComponent.cmd, "COMP=<component-name>" Typical arguments:
 COMP: component file name (required) EC_COMP_TYPE: hardware descriptor (for example EL7037); defaults from addSlave.cmd context COMP_S_ID: slave bus position; defaults from addSlave.cmd context CH_ID: channel index (default 1) MACROS: optional component or slave macros  What applyComponent.cmd does applyComponent.cmd executes a fixed pipeline:
 Loads component data (${ecmccomp_DIR}${COMP}.cmd). Loads slave/type support data (${ecmccomp_DIR}${EC_COMP_TYPE}_${COMP_TYPE}.cmd). Runs generic validation (validateGeneric.cmd). Validates custom macros (validateMacros.cmd). Runs component-type validation (validate<COMP_TYPE>.cmd). Applies SDO/config script (${SLAVE_SCRIPT}_${COMP_TYPE}.cmd). Runs cleanup scripts.  Typical usage with ecmccfg Use ecmccomp directly after addSlave.cmd:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd, "SLAVE_ID=8, HW_DESC=EL7037" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccomp_DIR}applyComponent.cmd, "COMP=Motor-OrientalMotor-PK267JB-Parallel" Explicit call variant:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccomp_DIR}applyComponent.cmd, "COMP_S_ID=12,EC_COMP_TYPE=EL7037,COMP=Motor-OrientalMotor-PK267JB-Parallel,CH_ID=1,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=500,I_STDBY_MA=100'" Notes  ecmccomp complements ecmccfg: use ecmccfg for system and axis startup flow, and ecmccomp for reusable component-level slave configuration. Supported macro sets depend on component and slave type; check the corresponding .cmd files in the ecmccomp repository.

title: Motion sequencer
content:
Scope The motion sequencer defines and executes short deterministic workflows inside the ecmc realtime loop. Sequences may be defined from IOC startup commands or edited at runtime through a dedicated asyn port and EPICS records.
This implementation is experimental. It is intended for workflows such as:
 move, wait for an input, then halt reusable scan-line sequences nested sequences for raster scans position-based output triggers time-based output triggers software triggers exposed as an EPICS counter  Existing axis behavior is unchanged unless a sequence is explicitly created, compiled, armed, and started.
Adding a Sequence Use addMotionSequence.cmd to create an empty sequence and its EPICS interface before defining steps:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}scripts/addMotionSequence.cmd, \  "SEQ_ID=0,MAX_STEPS=32,DB_PREFIX=$(IOC):,RECORD_PREFIX=Seq0-" Defaults:
 SEQ_ID=0 MAX_STEPS=32 ASYN_PORT=ECMC_SEQ<SEQ_ID> DB_PREFIX=$(IOC): RECORD_PREFIX=Seq<SEQ_ID>- SCAN=.1 second PREC=3 LOAD_PVS=1 REPORT=0  SOFT_TRG_FLNK optionally defines a forward link from the soft-trigger counter.
The wrapper first executes:
Cfg.CreateMotionSeq(seqIndex,maxSteps,portName) and then loads ecmcMotionSequence.template. Creation must happen before the records connect to the dedicated sequence port.
Each call also registers the sequence in the IOC configuration namespace:
$(IOC):MCU-Cfg-SEQ-Cnt $(IOC):MCU-Cfg-SEQ-FrstObjId $(IOC):MCU-Cfg-SEQ<ID>-Pfx $(IOC):MCU-Cfg-SEQ<ID>-NxtObjId $(IOC):MCU-Cfg-SEQ<ID>-PrvObjId The linked list preserves creation order and supports sparse sequence IDs. The caQtDM overview follows this list, so it only includes configured sequences. Open it through ecmcMain.ui or directly with:
python3 /ioc/modules/qt/ecmc_start_motion_sequence_overview.py <IOC> Lifecycle A sequence follows this lifecycle:
create -> define/edit -> compile -> arm -> start Typical startup definition:
Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(0,0,1,10.0,5.0,20.0,20.0,5000) Cfg.SeqWaitInPos(0,1,1,2000) Cfg.CompileMotionSeq(0) Cfg.ArmMotionSeq(0) The sequence can then be started through:
Cfg.StartMotionSeq(0) or the Seq0-Cmd-Start record.
Compile validates steps and resolves data-item bindings in a low-priority EPICS thread. Arm copies the compiled plan into the active realtime plan.
Runtime PV Editing Steps can also be inspected and changed through records. Select a step for readback with Read-Index and process Read-Cmd, or use Read-Prev and Read-Next:
caput IOC:Seq0-Read-Index 3 caput IOC:Seq0-Read-Cmd 1 caget IOC:Seq0-Read-Action IOC:Seq0-Read-Axis IOC:Seq0-Read-Name Read-Prev and Read-Next skip disabled/unconfigured step slots. Direct Read-Index plus Read-Cmd can still inspect any slot, including empty gaps left for sparse step numbering.
Read-CmdLine exposes the selected step as a one-line text row. It is a read-only waveform so navigating with Read-Prev and Read-Next does not overwrite the editable command buffer. Process Read-ToCmdLine to copy the selected row into CmdLine and the editable step fields:
caget -S IOC:Seq0-Read-CmdLine caput IOC:Seq0-Read-ToCmdLine 1 To edit a step, write the Edit-* fields and then process Edit-Apply. Recompile and arm the sequence before starting it:
caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Index 3 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Enable 1 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Action 5 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Axis 1 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Position 0.2 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Velocity 0.5 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Acceleration 2 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Deceleration 2 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-TimeoutMs 5000 caput -S IOC:Seq0-Edit-Name "rel +0.2" caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Apply 1 caput IOC:Seq0-Cmd-Compile 1 caput IOC:Seq0-Cmd-Arm 1 To insert or delete a configured step at Edit-Index, process Edit-Insert or Edit-Delete:
caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Index 4 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Insert 1 caput IOC:Seq0-Edit-Delete 1 Insert shifts steps at and after the index up by one and clears the inserted step. Delete shifts later steps down by one. Both operations invalidate the compiled/armed plan. Branch and goto targets are updated automatically when they are shifted. Delete fails if another step targets the deleted step.
The caQtDM sequence detail panel exposes the same readback and edit records. Edit-Action, Read-Action, and the runtime Action record are numeric action IDs. Use Read-CmdLine or CmdLine when a decoded text representation is more useful.
For common edits, use the one-line command waveform instead of writing every field manually:
caput -S IOC:Seq0-CmdLine "4: wait_item ec.s2.ai01 gt 10.5 timeout=5000 name='wait ai01'" caput IOC:Seq0-CmdLine-Apply 1 caget -S IOC:Seq0-CmdLine-Result caget -S IOC:Seq0-Read-CmdLine CmdLine-Result reports parse/apply feedback. Read-CmdLine exposes the selected readback row in the same one-line syntax.
The command line syntax is:
