<step>: <action> key=value key=value ... Use enabled=0 to define a disabled step. For power, enable=0|1 controls the axis power state.
Supported initial actions include:
nop reset axis=<id> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> power axis=<id> enable=<0|1> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> home axis=<id> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> move_abs axis=<id> pos=<pos> vel=<vel> acc=<acc> dec=<dec> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> move_rel axis=<id> dist=<dist> vel=<vel> acc=<acc> dec=<dec> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> move_vel axis=<id> vel=<vel> acc=<acc> dec=<dec> halt axis=<id> timeout=<ms> wait=<0|1> wait_inpos axis=<id> timeout=<ms> set_enc_homed axis=<id> homed=<0|1> wait_time ms=<ms> run_seq seq=<childSeq> timeout=<ms> set_item item=<dataItem> value=<value> wait_item item=<dataItem> op=<eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte> value=<value> timeout=<ms> exit_item item=<dataItem> op=<eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte> value=<value> timeout=<ms> branch_item item=<dataItem> op=<eq|ne|gt|gte|lt|lte> value=<value> true_step=<step> [false_step=<step>] goto_step target=<step> Supported Actions    ID Action     0 NOP   1 MC_Reset   2 MC_Power   3 MC_Home   4 MC_MoveAbsolute   5 MC_MoveRelative   6 WaitInPosition   7 SetItem   8 WaitItem   9 WaitTime   10 RunSequence   11 ArmPositionTrigger   12 WaitTriggerDone   13 ArmTimeTrigger   14 MC_MoveVelocity   15 MC_Halt   16 ExitItem   17 SetEncHomed   18 BranchItem   19 GotoStep    Prefer the action-specific Cfg.Seq* commands when defining sequences in a startup script.
Startup Commands Motion and waits:
Cfg.SeqNop(seq,step) Cfg.SeqWaitTime(seq,step,waitMs) Cfg.SeqReset(seq,step,axis,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqReset(seq,step,axis,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqPower(seq,step,axis,enable,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqPower(seq,step,axis,enable,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqHome(seq,step,axis,homeSeq,homePos,velToCam,velOffCam,acc,dec,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqHome(seq,step,axis,homeSeq,homePos,velToCam,velOffCam,acc,dec,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(seq,step,axis,pos,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(seq,step,axis,pos,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqMoveRel(seq,step,axis,distance,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqMoveRel(seq,step,axis,distance,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqMoveVel(seq,step,axis,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqMoveVel(seq,step,axis,vel,acc,dec,timeoutMs,wait,tolerance) Cfg.SeqHalt(seq,step,axis,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqHalt(seq,step,axis,timeoutMs,wait) Cfg.SeqWaitInPos(seq,step,axis,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqSetEncHomed(seq,step,axis,homed) SeqSetEncHomed sets the homed flag on the axis primary/current encoder and then advances immediately.
Data items:
Cfg.SeqSetItem(seq,step,item,value,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqWaitItem(seq,step,item,op,value,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqExitItem(seq,step,item,op,value,timeoutMs) Cfg.SeqBranchItem(seq,step,item,op,value,trueStep) Cfg.SeqBranchItem(seq,step,item,op,value,trueStep,falseStep) Cfg.SeqGotoStep(seq,step,targetStep) Cfg.InsertMotionSeqStep(seq,step) Cfg.DeleteMotionSeqStep(seq,step) SeqWaitItem and SeqExitItem support ==, !=, >, >=, <, <=, eq, and ne. SeqExitItem exits the current sequence as Done when the condition is fulfilled; if the condition is false, the sequence continues with the next step.
SeqBranchItem uses the same operators. It jumps to trueStep when the condition is fulfilled. In one-line commands these targets are named true_step and false_step. If falseStep/false_step is omitted, a false condition continues with the next enabled step; otherwise it jumps to the false target. Branch and goto targets are configured step IDs and must point to enabled steps.
Nested sequences:
Cfg.SeqRunSeq(parentSeq,step,childSeq,timeoutMs) Triggers:
Cfg.SeqArmPosTrigger(seq,step,id,axis,item,startPos,interval,endPos,value,pulseMs) Cfg.SeqArmTimeTrigger(seq,step,id,item,delayMs,periodMs,count,value,pulseMs) Cfg.SeqWaitTriggerDone(seq,step,id,timeoutMs) Control and inspection:
Cfg.CompileMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.ArmMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.StartMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.StopMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.ResetMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.ReportMotionSeq(seq) Cfg.ReportMotionSeq(seq,step) Velocity Move and Halt The short SeqMoveVel form is nonblocking. It issues the velocity command and advances immediately:
Cfg.SeqMoveVel(0,0,1,10.0,20.0,20.0,1000) Cfg.SeqWaitItem(0,1,ec0.s1.stopInput,==,1,30000) Cfg.SeqHalt(0,2,1,5000) The extended form optionally waits for actual velocity:
Cfg.SeqMoveVel(0,0,1,10.0,20.0,20.0,5000,1,0.1) This waits until actual velocity is within 10.0 +/- 0.1. Internally the generic step arguments are:
wait=1;tol=0.1 This representation is also available through the Edit-Args record.
Blocking and Nonblocking Motion All motion helpers support an optional final wait argument. The short forms keep their existing defaults:
 reset, power, home, absolute move, relative move, and halt default to wait=1 velocity move defaults to wait=0  With wait=0, the command is issued and the sequence advances immediately. This allows multiple axes to be started in consecutive realtime cycles:
Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(0,0,1,100.0,10.0,20.0,20.0,1000,0) Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(0,1,2,50.0,5.0,10.0,10.0,1000,0) Cfg.SeqWaitInPos(0,2,1,15000) Cfg.SeqWaitInPos(0,3,2,15000) The generic step representation stores this as:
wait=0 It can therefore also be configured through Edit-Args. A later wait step should be used when completion must be synchronized.
Nested Sequences Sequence 1 can execute sequence 0, wait, and execute it again:
Cfg.SeqRunSeq(1,0,0,10000) Cfg.SeqWaitTime(1,1,500) Cfg.SeqRunSeq(1,2,0,10000) step is the step position in the parent sequence. childSeq selects the sequence being called.
The child must reach DONE before the parent step timeout. Child errors and stops propagate to the parent. Direct self-call is rejected during compile.
Position Triggers Position triggers are armed before a later motion step and execute in the background:
Cfg.SeqArmPosTrigger(0,0,0,1,ec0.s1.output01,10.0,1.0,29.0,1,5) Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(0,1,1,50.0,10.0,20.0,20.0,10000) Cfg.SeqWaitTriggerDone(0,2,0,1000) This pulses the output at positions 10, 11, through 29. The range is startPos:interval:endPos; negative intervals support reverse motion, for example 80,-1,20 fires at 80,79,...,20.
Time Triggers Time triggers use elapsed time after the arm step:
Cfg.SeqArmTimeTrigger(0,0,0,ec0.s1.output01,10,5,100,1,1) This fires first after 10 ms, then every 5 ms, for 100 pulses. Each pulse remains high for 1 ms.
Soft Triggers Use soft instead of a data-item name:
Cfg.SeqArmPosTrigger(0,0,0,1,soft,10.0,1.0,29.0,1,0) Cfg.SeqArmTimeTrigger(0,1,1,soft,10,5,100,1,0) Each soft trigger event increments:
stat.soft_trigger_count All trigger events, both hard and soft, also update:
stat.trigger_count stat.trigger_id Trigger IDs 0..7 expose dedicated counters and pulse-active status:
stat.soft_trigger.<id>.count stat.soft_trigger.<id>.pulse The internal asyn names keep the original soft_trigger prefix for compatibility, but these per-ID counters now count both hard and soft trigger IDs. The ecmccfg database maps them to Trigger0Count/Trigger0Pulse through Trigger7Count/Trigger7Pulse, and keeps the old SoftTrig0Count/SoftTrig0Pulse aliases for compatibility. Use the counters as the reliable EPICS event source. The pulse flags are only high while a trigger pulse is active and therefore require a nonzero pulseMs.
and updates:
stat.soft_trigger_id The corresponding soft-only records are SoftTriggerCount and SoftTriggerId. SoftTriggerEvent is processed through a CP link when the counter posts a changed value. SOFT_TRG_FLNK can forward-link that event to another record. The counter value should still be used to detect the number of new events.
EPICS Record Interface With defaults for sequence 0, records use prefix $(IOC):Seq0-.
Editing:
Edit-Index Edit-Enable Edit-Action Edit-Axis Edit-Position Edit-Velocity Edit-Acceleration Edit-Deceleration Edit-TimeoutMs Edit-Name Edit-Transition Edit-OnError Edit-Args Edit-Apply CmdLine CmdLine-Apply CmdLine-Result Readback navigation:
Read-Index Read-Cmd Read-Prev Read-Next Read-Enable Read-Action Read-Axis Read-Position Read-Velocity Read-Acceleration Read-Deceleration Read-TimeoutMs Read-Name Read-Transition Read-OnError Read-Args Commands and status:
Cmd-Compile Cmd-Arm Cmd-Start Cmd-Stop Cmd-Reset State Valid Armed Running CompileBusy StepIndex Action ErrorId StepCount ElapsedMs StepName ErrorText ValidationText TriggerId TriggerCount TriggerEvent Trigger0Count..Trigger7Count Trigger0Pulse..Trigger7Pulse Trigger0Event..Trigger7Event SoftTriggerId SoftTriggerCount SoftTriggerEvent SoftTrig0Count..SoftTrig7Count SoftTrig0Pulse..SoftTrig7Pulse SoftTrig0Event..SoftTrig7Event Status and readback records poll at SCAN because realtime sequence updates do not currently generate asyn callbacks.
PLC Functions The ecmc PLC library exposes sequence control and status helpers. Command-style functions are rising-edge triggered on the execute argument.
seq_arm(seq,execute) seq_set_step(seq,execute,step_id) seq_arm arms an already compiled sequence. seq_set_step requests a jump to a configured step ID. The sequence must be armed or running; missing target steps put the sequence in error.
Status getters:
seq_get_state(seq) seq_get_valid(seq) seq_get_armed(seq) seq_get_running(seq) seq_get_compile_busy(seq) seq_get_step(seq) seq_get_action(seq) seq_get_error(seq) seq_get_step_count(seq) seq_get_elapsed_ms(seq) seq_get_step returns the configured step ID of the active step. It returns -1 when no step is active.
Example:
arm_err := seq_arm(0, arm_exec); jump_err := seq_set_step(0, jump_exec, 20); seq_running := seq_get_running(0); seq_step := seq_get_step(0); Example: Reusable Scan Line Define sequence 0 as one X scan line:
Cfg.SeqArmPosTrigger(0,0,0,1,soft,10.0,1.0,109.0,1,0) Cfg.SeqMoveAbs(0,1,1,110.0,20.0,50.0,50.0,20000) Cfg.SeqWaitTriggerDone(0,2,0,2000) Cfg.CompileMotionSeq(0) Cfg.ArmMotionSeq(0) Sequence 1 composes scan lines with Y steps:
Cfg.SeqRunSeq(1,0,0,25000) Cfg.SeqMoveRel(1,1,2,0.1,2.0,10.0,10.0,5000) Cfg.SeqRunSeq(1,2,0,25000) Separate forward and backward child sequences can implement a snake/raster scan without an extra return move.
Current Limitations  This implementation still needs build and target-system testing. Status records use polling rather than realtime asyn callbacks. The EPICS records expose the generic step structure; action-specific operator screens can be added in the EPICS layer. Compile currently uses one low-priority worker thread per sequence. Recursive call validation rejects direct self-call, not complete recursive sequence graphs. Soft triggers expose a shared counter and last trigger ID rather than an event FIFO. Trigger timing resolution is one ecmc realtime cycle.

title: Nanotec N6 EtherCAT drive
content:
Scope and status This page describes the ecmccfg and ecmccomp support for the Nanotec N6-1-1-1-S EtherCAT drive with FIR-v2508 firmware. The supplied ESI is PLC_N6-1-1-1-S_2508-B1072143_N6-1-1-1-S.xml.
Relevant files are:
 hardware/Nanotec/ecmcN6-1-1-1-S.cmd db/Nanotec/ecmcN6-1-1-1-S.substitutions qt/ecmcN6-1-1-1-S.ui qt/ecmcN6-1-1-1-S_expert.ui ecmccomp component type N6, implemented by N6_2PH_STEPPER.cmd  The N6 hardware configuration and panels are currently marked untested. Commission with conservative current settings and verify every safety-related input and drive reaction on the actual machine.
 Motor configuration The ecmccomp configuration supports a generic two-phase open-loop stepper. The main component macros are:
   Macro Meaning Default or limit     I_MAX_MA Rated/run phase current in mA Required, drive limit 6000 mA   I_STDBY_MA Standstill phase current in mA Required   STEPS Full steps per mechanical revolution Motor value, normally 200   INV_DIR Invert position and velocity direction 0   I2T_MAX_MS Maximum-current duration 100 ms   CURR_RED_DLY_MS Delay before standstill-current reduction 1000 ms   N6_POS_UNIT CiA-402 object 0x60A8 0x00B50000   N6_VEL_UNIT CiA-402 object 0x60A9 0x00B50300   N6_IO_24V Select 24 V inputs and +UB outputs 1   N6_INPUT_PULLUP Select input pull-up instead of pull-down 0    U_NOM_MV, R_COIL_MOHM, and L_COIL_UH are accepted for compatibility with generic motor definitions. They are validated where applicable but are not written to the N6 for open-loop stepper operation. The resistance and inductance fields at 0x3380 belong to sensorless feedback and are not the ordinary open-loop stepper winding parameters.
For example:
I_MAX_MA=200,I_STDBY_MA=100,STEPS=200,INV_DIR=0 produces the following current settings:
   Object Value Result     0x6075 200 Rated/run current 200 mA   0x6073 1000 1000 per mille, maximum current 200 mA   0x3219:02 1000 Wait 1000 ms at zero setpoint   0x3219:03 500 500 per mille, standby current 100 mA    Standby reduction is automatic in open-loop mode when the commanded velocity in 0x60FF remains zero for the time in 0x3219:02. No additional enable bit is required.
The N6 does not provide motor overload or motor overtemperature protection in this open-loop setup. Nanotec also notes that sinusoidal commutation can cause a winding current up to sqrt(2) times the configured value for a period of time. Confirm whether the motor data-sheet current is the applicable bipolar phase-current rating and perform a temperature endurance test.
 Position and velocity scaling The default unit objects select the native, highest-resolution units:
0x60A8 = 0x00B50000 # encoder increments 0x60A9 = 0x00B50300 # encoder increments per second For an open-loop two-phase stepper, ecmccomp sets:
pole pairs = STEPS / 4 increments per revolution = pole pairs * 65536 = STEPS * 16384 For a 200-step motor:
pole pairs = 50 increments per revolution = 3276800 degrees per increment = 360 / 3276800 = 45 / 409600 Use the same numerical scaling magnitude for encoder position and drive velocity:
position: increments * 45/409600 = degrees velocity: increments/second * 45/409600 = degrees/second The time dimension remains unchanged, which is why position and velocity use the same conversion factor. Their resulting engineering units are different. Direction may additionally be inverted with INV_DIR or at axis level.
Cyclic PDO mapping The N6 supports configurable PDO mappings, but 0x1C13 has only four TxPDO assignment slots. Do not assign 0x1A04 or later as a fifth TxPDO: writing 0x1C13:05 aborts with 0x06090011, followed by Invalid input configuration.
The additional input entries are therefore packed into 0x1A03:
   Direction PDO Object ecmc entry     Output 0x1600 0x6040:00 driveControl01   Output 0x1600 0x6060:00 modeControl01   Output 0x1602 0x60FF:00 velocitySetpoint01   Output 0x1603 0x60FE:01 binaryOutputArray01   Input 0x1A00 0x6041:00 driveStatus01   Input 0x1A00 0x6061:00 modeActual01   Input 0x1A01 0x6064:00 positionActual01   Input 0x1A02 0x606C:00 velocityActual01   Input 0x1A03 0x60FD:00 binaryInputArray01   Input 0x1A03 0x60E4:03 positionActualInc01   Input 0x1A03 0x60E4:04 positionActualSSI01   Input 0x1A03 0x603F:00 errorCode01   Input 0x1A03 0x6077:00 torqueActual01    The incremental and SSI velocity objects 0x60E5:03/04 are intentionally not mapped. Objects 0x33A0 and 0x33B0 configure the incremental and SSI interfaces; they are not the cyclic position values. The attached encoder’s resolution and protocol still require device-specific SDO configuration.
Exposed EPICS process variables The dedicated N6 panels use the following main PVs:
   PV suffix Content     Drv01-VelAct Main actual velocity   Drv01-TrqAct Actual torque, scaled by 0.1 percent   Drv01-Stat CiA-402 statusword   Drv01-ErrCode CiA-402 error code from 0x603F   Enc01-PosAct Main motor position from 0x6064   Inc01-PosAct Incremental-interface position   SSI01-PosAct SSI-interface position   BI01-Arr Complete 32-bit 0x60FD input word   BO01-Arr Complete 32-bit 0x60FE:01 output word   BO01-Arr-RB Output-word readback    N6-specific database templates use a 0xFFFFFFFF asyn mask. The generic binary-array templates use only 0xFFFF and must not be substituted here, because the N6 physical I/O bits are above bit 15.
Digital inputs and ecmc limit handling The configuration explicitly writes 0x323A:01=1 and 0x323A:02=0. The inputs therefore use 24 V thresholds with pull-down wiring. The voltage-level selector is shared with the outputs, so outputs 1 through 3 use +UB rather than 5 V. Override these values with N6_IO_24V and N6_INPUT_PULLUP only when the connected electrical interface requires it.
BI01-Arr exposes two kinds of signals:
   Bit Meaning     0 N6 internal negative-limit function   1 N6 internal positive-limit function   2 N6 internal home function   3 N6 internal interlock function   16 Physical input 1   17 Physical input 2   18 Physical input 3   19 Physical input 4   20 Physical input 5   21–23 Other/reserved routed sources in this variant   24 Physical input 6    For normal ecmc handling, use physical bits 16 through 20 and 24. For example, ecmc can use bit 16 as the negative axis limit and bit 17 as the positive axis limit.
Object 0x3242 controls the N6 internal input routing. Its factory values for subindices 1 through 4 are zero, meaning that the internal NLS, PLS, home and interlock bits are sourced from constant zero. This leaves the physical inputs available as ordinary inputs and lets ecmc implement the reaction.
0x3242 is savable. A drive previously configured by another application may not have its factory routing. To guarantee ecmc-only handling, verify or write 0x3242:01, :02, :03, and :04 to zero. Merely exposing BI01-Arr does not connect its physical bits to the ecmc axis limits; configure the axis interlocks explicitly.
 If internal drive handling is deliberately enabled, 0x3701 selects the reaction. The factory value -1 only records the limit position. Values 1 and 5 use the normal deceleration ramp; values 2 and 6 use the quick-stop ramp. This internal behavior is separate from ecmc limit handling.
Digital outputs BO01-Arr maps the complete 0x60FE:01 word:
   Bit Meaning     0 Brake output control   16 Physical output 1   17 Physical output 2   18 Physical output 3    Output routing is configured in 0x3252. The factory mapping routes outputs 1 through 3 to 0x60FE:01 bits 16 through 18. As with input routing, verify saved settings on a drive that may have been configured previously.
Optional raw position and periodic outputs N6-1-1-1-S_OPT offers optional raw 6063 position alongside the existing 6064 mapping. With the ecmccomp Drive-Generic-PositionOutput component, this supports the commissioned open-loop 100-full-step output while the axis retains fine counter feedback. See N6 optional configuration for options, startup order, 5 V/24 V I/O selection, output gates, panels, method-35 homing PDOs, global-PLC triggering and the firmware-specific test scope.
Useful commissioning checks Adjust master and slave position as required:
ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint32 0x3202 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type int32 0x60FF 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint32 0x6075 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x6073 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x3219 2 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x3219 3 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type int16 0x3701 0 Expected for open-loop standstill are 0x3202=0 and 0x60FF=0.
Related pages  Hardware knowledge base Motion scaling ecmccomp

title: Simulation backend (SIM=1)
content:
SIM=1 selects ECMC’s memory-backed I/O driver for the selected master ID. Slave and entry declarations create typed memory instead of configuring a physical EtherCAT master. Motion, PLCs, limits, interlocks and master/slave coordination continue running in the IOC’s normal realtime cycle.
The memory driver is not a device model. It does not automatically turn drive commands into enabled feedback or encoder movement. A separate Python model, PLC, manual PV client or other model must supply those inputs.
Start an IOC in simulation mode Pass SIM=1 when loading ecmccfg:
require ecmccfg "MASTER_ID=0,SIM=1,EC_RATE=1000" # Load slave, entry, axis and PLC configuration as usual.    Setting Behavior     SIM=0 or omitted Existing physical EtherCAT backend   SIM=1 with MASTER_ID>=0 Memory backend for that instance   MASTER_ID=-1 Existing masterless operation; does not create a simulated master    Startup selects the backend before claiming the instance and skips MX-System hardware discovery in simulation mode. Backend selection is configuration-only; choose it before creating that instance’s objects. Restart with the appropriate startup arguments to switch an existing IOC between real and simulated I/O.
For manual ECMC configuration, the corresponding selection is:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetSampleRate(1000)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetIoBackend(0,1)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.EcSetMaster(0)" Set the sample rate before creating objects. Signal names such as ec0.s14.positionActual01 stay unchanged, so the normal motion and PLC links bind the selected backend’s storage. Mixed real/simulated instances use distinct IDs and explicit backend selection; SIM=1 is not a global override for other instances. This does not add support for multiple physical EtherCAT masters.
The main ecmccfg panel shows SIMULATED in amber or REAL in green from $(P)MCU-Cfg-Sim-Mode. That PV describes the startup SIM setting; it is not a runtime backend selector or an inventory of manually configured mixed instances.
Generated simulation PVs The normal setAppMode.cmd/finalize path automatically generates simulation field records before runtime when SIM=1. Their default prefix is ${ECMC_PREFIX}SIM:. For example, an IOC prefix SIMSLIT: produces:
   Field direction Writable PV Readback PV     Input to ECMC: status, position, switches SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveStatus01 Same name with -RB   Output from ECMC: control word, setpoint SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveControl01-Set SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveControl01    These are raw I/O values, not axis engineering values. Position fields normally contain encoder counts, and control/status fields contain native bit words. Signed, unsigned, floating-point and 64-bit fields keep their declared types. Do not assume that writing 1 to a position field means 1 mm.
# Observe the control word produced by ECMC. caget SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveControl01 # Inject a status word into the simulated input memory. caput SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveStatus01 3 caget SIMSLIT:SIM:ec0:s14:driveStatus01-RB The status value above is manual bit injection, not a complete drive model. An output -Set write is also a single write: its axis or PLC owner may replace it in the next cycle. There is no persistent force/override mode.
The records use automatically created dedicated asyn ports such as MC_CPU1_SIM0, separate from the main MC_CPU1 parameter table. They share the same I/O buffers; no second I/O image or additional IOC RT thread is introduced. Normal axis, PLC and legacy entry parameters remain on the main port.
For a custom prefix, set ECMC_SIM_PREFIX before adding slaves, so discovery aliases and generated field records agree. A manually configured IOC can call Cfg.SimLoadRecords(<prefix>) after entry declarations and before runtime or iocInit. Only declared realtime scalar fields at nonnegative slave positions are generated; aliases and built-in ZERO/ONE do not create duplicate PVs.
External Python models and GUI The tools are in the ecmccfg repository, under tools/simulation/. Install PyEpics in the client environment and use the normal Channel Access network settings, including EPICS_CA_ADDR_LIST when needed. Start the SIM IOC first, then run these commands from the ecmccfg repository root:
python3 -m pip install pyepics # Read-only inventory of supported and unsupported configured slaves. python3 tools/simulation/ioc.py --prefix SIMSLIT:SIM: --list # Run models for supported drives; observe manual terminal fields. python3 tools/simulation/ioc.py --prefix SIMSLIT:SIM: # Optional Tk window with live values and editable simulation fields. python3 tools/simulation/ioc.py --prefix SIMSLIT:SIM: --gui Discovery follows FirstSlave, ecN:sM:HWType and ecN:sM:NxtObjId aliases under that single prefix. It reuses normal ecmccfg slave metadata, which must remain enabled (DEFAULT_SLAVE_PVS=true). Unsupported types are listed and left untouched. Use --slave 14 to select a slave, --master N for another master, and --settings models.json for per-slave scaling and behavior.
   Hardware family Tool support     EL7031 variants, EL7041, EL7041-0052, EL7047 Basic stepper velocity-mode model   E*72xx, including supported EL/EP/ELM variants DS402 CSV/CSP model   EL7062, ED7062, MO7062 family Independent configured DS402 channels 01/02   EL1004, EL1008, EL1808, EL1809 Manual digital input injection   EL2004, EL2008, EL2808 Digital output readback and single-write controls   EL5042, EL5102, EL5101 variants Manual raw encoder/status fields    Support also requires compatible configured fields and record types. CST/CSTCA, drive-motion-control modes, EL7047 position-interface variants and oversampling arrays are not modeled. Standalone encoder terminals are not automatically coupled to a drive: supply their feedback relationship in your model.
The GUI shows slave type, command/feedback values and model status. Writable fields can be edited manually, including drive feedback and output -Set PVs. Active models or PLCs may overwrite those edits. Tkinter and a graphical display are required only for --gui; headless operation remains available.
Scaling and enable delays Stepper defaults are 2000 full steps/s at full-scale signed velocity, a 200-step/revolution motor, and 12800 encoder counts/revolution. For example:
{ "ec0.s14": { "full_steps_per_second": 2000, "motor_steps_per_rev": 200, "encoder_counts_per_rev": 12800, "enable_delay": 0.05 } } The DS402 model has separate position and velocity scaling. Defaults match the repository servo example: 2^20 counts/revolution and 2^31 velocity units for 8000 revolutions/s. Override these for the configured motor and drive mode; scaling is not discovered from SDOs. If CSV and CSP command fields both exist, select the model mode explicitly in the settings file.
Stepper enable acknowledgement defaults to 50 ms; DS402 forward handshake transitions default to 10 ms each. CA transport, polling and scheduling add variable delay. A model error or normal shutdown makes a best-effort fault write that removes enabled feedback. A disconnected or forcibly killed client cannot guarantee delivery. Use one model writer per drive; do not run the discovery models alongside a test plant that owns the same signals.
Configuration support and limitations The backend stores scalar PDO declarations, aliases and many configuration settings in memory. Scalar/configured SDO writes store object-dictionary bytes; they do not perform mailbox transactions or run device reset logic. Supported SDO reads/verifications use those stored bytes. DC, watchdog and timing settings retain configuration metadata without reproducing hardware timing.
Unsupported services, including memory maps, asynchronous SDO requests, SoE and some specialized link/timing commands, report ERROR_MAIN_IO_CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED. Arbitrary hardware configurations are not guaranteed to load unchanged.
The driver does not test PDO byte offsets, physical bit packing, endianness, distributed clocks, network faults, electrical behavior or real drive dynamics. Python feedback is asynchronous, not cycle-synchronous. Passing a functional simulation test does not validate real EtherCAT timing or hardware behavior.
Explicit instance-health injection is available with Cfg.SimSetHealthy(0,0) and recovery with Cfg.SimSetHealthy(0,1). Cfg.SimSetValue(ec0.s14.positionActual01,123) injects a typed scalar directly. An unhealthy instance blocks its bindings/startup readiness; this is not an emulation of EtherCAT’s missed-frame filtering. Physical domain-failure tolerance remains unchanged.
Dedicated slit acceptance tests The separate configuration tests/integration/slit/ioc/ provides a simulation-only slit IOC with its own SIMSLIT: namespace. The colocated modular integration runner supplies its coupled plant:
# From the ecmccfg repository root, with the dedicated IOC already running. python3 tests/integration/slit/run.py --prefix SIMSLIT: --run The default run includes open and closed loop. Select groups with, for example, --case limits, --case homing, --case isolation or --case target_write. The suite covers motion, limits, faults, encoder feedback/noise, brakes, reduced torque, synchronization, native/motor interfaces and homing. See tests/integration/slit/README.md and tools/simulation/README.md in ecmccfg for setup, selection, reports, model settings and applicability limits.
This backend is separate from the local dummy entries described under Simulation entries. Local ZERO, ONE and EcAddSimEntry values can also be used in a physical IOC.

title: ecb
content:
ecb (ECMC Configuration Builder, https://github.com/paulscherrerinstitute/ecb) is a C++ YAML validation and rendering tool that can be used as backend for the ecmccfg YAML loaders.
What it is for  Validating YAML data against schema definitions Rendering ecmccfg Jinja-style templates without the Python venv pipeline Reading and updating YAML keys (readkey, updatekey) used by loader scripts  How it fits with ecmccfg ecb is used by loadYamlAxis.cmd, loadYamlPlc.cmd, and loadYamlEnc.cmd when:
epicsEnvSet(ECMC_CFG_TOOL, "ecb") The ecb module startup file sets this automatically.
ecmccfg still provides schema and template files (for example ecbSchema.json, axis_main.jinja2, plc.jinja2); ecb is the validation/rendering engine.
Notes  Default backend remains jinja if ECMC_CFG_TOOL is not set to ecb. Using ecb avoids Python venv/pip dependency during YAML parsing. ecb supports the subset of Jinja syntax needed by ecmccfg templates (implemented via Inja, with ecb-specific compatibility handling). Controller YAML settings, including controller.resetIAtRmp and controller.freezeIAtRmp, use the same generated configuration commands with either the ecb or jinja backend. For CLI details and schema behavior, see the ecb repository documentation.  Optional post-homing move For both homing and encoder.homing, postMoveEnable: false does not require postMovePosition. If a target is supplied, it is retained in the generated configuration; zero and EPICS macro targets are supported.
When postMoveEnable: true, specify postMovePosition. The shared templates emit an explicit error and ecmcExit if it is missing, before enabling the post-homing move. This behavior is the same for the Python and ECB renderers; the missing-target rejection occurs in the generated startup script.
Regression test (with the Python dependencies and ECB installed):
ECB=/path/to/ecb python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_homing_post_move.py -v

title: Nanotec N6 optional PDOs, position output and homing
content:
The N6 optional configuration combines fine open-loop axis feedback with a periodic digital output generated inside the drive. Optional homing PDOs prepare the interface for referencing the output’s position source using homing method 35.
The working bench setup was an N6-1-1-1-S, firmware FIR-v2542-B1080909, with a 200-full-step motor in cyclic synchronous velocity mode (CSV). Fine counter feedback and an output every 100 full steps were demonstrated together. Subsequent method-35 testing returned scaled position to zero and produced a repeatable first-edge shift, documented below. Full homing/error handling still needs commissioning. Homing is commanded through the normal axis interface and does not execute automatically at IOC startup.
Configure the hardware and components Build/install both updated modules: ecmccfg supplies the hardware, records and panels; ecmccomp supplies Drive-Generic-PositionOutput.
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addSlave.cmd "HW_DESC=N6-1-1-1-S_OPT,OPT='RAW_POS=1,HOMING=1'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Motor-Generic-2Phase-Stepper,CH_ID=1,MACROS='I_MAX_MA=400,I_STDBY_MA=100,STEPS=200,INV_DIR=0'" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Drive-Generic-PositionOutput,CH_ID=1,MACROS='FULL_STEPS=100,OUTPUT=1,ARM=1,N6_IO_24V=0'" Apply the motor first, then the position-output component, before applying EtherCAT configuration. The output component checks the raw mapping, motor configuration and supported interval. Motor INV_DIR=0 is required. Applying the motor again after the output component is rejected because it would restore position units and change the output period.
The complete example is examples/PSI/lab_setup/N6/startup_position_output_100_steps.cmd, with cfg/axis_position_output.yaml for the axis. The ordinary startup.cmd remains available for the base configuration. Restart the IOC after changing PDO options. The former N6-1-1-1-S_POS_OUT hardware wrapper has been removed; use _OPT instead.
Hardware options and PDO names    Option Default Effect when set to 1     RAW_POS 0 Map fine 6063:00 as positionActual01; name existing 6064:00 entry positionActualScaled01   HOMING 0 Add method, offset, drive homing speeds/acceleration and the sequence-26 trigger alias   CAPTURE 0 Map 3241:01–0C capture control readbacks, counts and latched positions   ANALOG_IN 0 Map both signed 3320:01–02 analog input values    All options are independent and accept only 0 or 1. With all disabled, the PDO mapping matches the base N6-1-1-1-S configuration. The motor component type remains N6.
RAW_POS=1 appends the S32 6063 entry to existing TxPDO 1A03, increasing that PDO from 16 to 20 bytes. The four TxPDO assignment slots are retained. HOMING=1 appends 17 bytes to existing RxPDO 1603, increasing it from 4 to 21 bytes without adding an RxPDO assignment slot. These options map entries; they do not change position units, route outputs or execute homing. The trigger alias is process-image data over existing controlword bit 4; it adds no EtherCAT PDO bytes.
Capture and analog input options The runnable all-options example is examples/PSI/lab_setup/N6/startup_opt_all.cmd. It reuses the 100-step startup and M1 axis with N6_CAPTURE=1,N6_ANALOG_IN=1.
To enable all optional mappings directly:
HW_DESC=N6-1-1-1-S_OPT,OPT='RAW_POS=1,HOMING=1,CAPTURE=1,ANALOG_IN=1' CAPTURE=1 exposes all twelve 3241 payload subindices as U32 readbacks:
   Group Source Subindices PDO Entry suffix     01 Home-switch capture 01–04 1A00 01   02 Input 3 capture 05–08 1A01 02   03 Input 4 capture 09–0C 1A02 03    Each group has captureControlNN, captureCountNN, capturePositionNN and captureRawPositionNN. Corresponding PVs are CaptureNN-Control-RB, CaptureNN-Count, CaptureNN-PosAct and CaptureNN-PosRaw. Position is in configured drive position units; raw position is in sensor increments. The EPICS records preserve the entire unsigned 32-bit range. For negative positions, interpret the appropriate 32-bit two’s-complement value in the application rather than treating the unsigned display as a distance.
The object dictionary marks these subindices TxPDO-only, including the control fields. Mapping them does not arm capture or change input routing. Configure the desired edge by SDO: 3241:01 for the home-switch source, :05 for input 3, :09 for input 4. Values are 0 disabled, 1 rising, 2 falling and 3 both edges. Re-arming can reset the capture count. For example, enable both-edge capture of input 3 on master 1/slave 0:
ethercat download -m1 -p0 --type uint32 0x3241 0x05 3 Check capture/input-routing behavior with the actual wiring and firmware; in particular, its raw sensor value needs verification with our generated open-loop counter. No automatic capture SDO writes are added by _OPT.
ANALOG_IN=1 maps analogInput01 and analogInput02 (S32, 3320:01–02) in 1A03, with PVs AI01 and AI02. Values use the drive’s existing input scaling and offsets. The records label them user, not volts; no voltage conversion or analog-input configuration is applied by this option.
The groups are deliberately spread across existing PDOs because each PDO has at most eight mapping entries. With all options enabled, TxPDO entry counts are 1A00:6, 1A01:5, 1A02:5, 1A03:8; the four assignment slots are retained. 1A03 is 28 bytes with raw position and both analog inputs.
Fine feedback and scaled output position    Configuration positionActual01 positionActualScaled01     Base descriptor or RAW_POS=0 6064, position in configured units Not mapped   _OPT, RAW_POS=1 6063, fine open-loop counter 6064, position in configured units    For the tested 200-full-step motor, the fine counter has nominally 3,276,800 counts/revolution, or 16,384 counts/full step. The example uses full-step engineering units:
epics: unit: steps drive: numerator: 200 denominator: 3276800 encoder: unit: steps numerator: 200 denominator: 3276800 bits: 32 position: ec0.s$(ENC_SID).positionActual01 These are excerpts from the full YAML; use the complete example when configuring an IOC and keep EtherCAT paths consistent with its axis configuration. For degrees, use numerator 360 for both drive and encoder and set both unit labels to deg. Check the corresponding scaling when using another motor step count. Velocity remains in native increments per second, so the drive and encoder scales remain matched.
The position-output component makes 6064 deliberately coarse: with FULL_STEPS=100, one count is 100 full steps, or half a revolution on this motor. Use 6063 for fine axis feedback. Both entries are available simultaneously, but only one is the fine counter after changing 60A8. The counter represents generated open-loop motion; it does not measure rotor position or detect lost steps. Additional 60E4 position values also use the configured position units; check external feedback channels if used. Its 32-bit rollover and the output’s behavior across rollover require application checks.
Configure periodic output triggering The output is generated inside the drive from scaled position 6064 and its digital-output divider. It requires no cyclic PLC pulse generation or NanoJ program. This configuration provides periodic position-related triggering; it does not program arbitrary absolute compare positions or a pulse width.
   Component macro Default Meaning     FULL_STEPS 100 Full motor steps per output pulse   OUTPUT 1 Physical digital output 1, 2 or 3   ARM 0 Initial output gate: 0 disabled, 1 enabled   N6_IO_24V 0 for the first output 0 = 5 V; 1 = nominal 24 V/+UB_Logic   N6_INPUT_PULLUP Inherit motor; normally 0 Shared input bias: 0 pull-down, 1 pull-up    Supported intervals are 10^n * d, where n=0..6 and d is one of 1,2,4,8,16,32,64. Other intervals, such as 50 or 125 full steps, are rejected. The component selects a canonical full-step unit 10^n and a power-of-two divider.
All outputs on one drive share 60A8. For example, 100 and 200 steps use the same unit of 100 with dividers 1 and 2, so they can coexist. Intervals 100 and 10 select different unit exponents and are rejected together. Electrical settings are shared too: later output components inherit the first output’s voltage and reject conflicting explicit voltage/bias choices. Intervals are startup settings, not live scan parameters. Nothing is saved to drive flash by this component.
For output 1 every 100 full steps, the important settings are:
   Object Value Purpose     60E6:01 0 Keep sensorless interface disabled   60A8:00 0x02AC0000 Position unit = 100 full steps   3252:02 0x0910 Route position divider 1 to output 1, gated by bit 16   323A:01 0 by default Select 5 V I/O   60FE:01, bit 16 ARM Output 1 gate    With 200 full steps/revolution, subsequent edges were observed 180 degrees apart: two output transitions per revolution. The expected steady time between edges is 100 / abs(velocity in full steps/second) seconds (or 180 / abs(velocity in degrees/second) when using degrees). An edge is not a complete pulse: alternating rising/falling edges 100 steps apart give a 200-step full cycle. See the observed first-edge shift after homing below; verify waveform, pulse width, stop/restart and reversal on the bench. The direct position-routing limit is 500 Hz.
Wiring and I/O voltage Output 1 is on X4 pin 5, with GNDD on X4 pin 8. The position-output component defaults to 5 V output levels. Select N6_IO_24V=1 for nominal 24 V/+UB_Logic instead.
323A:01 selects both the output level and the digital input thresholds. Selecting 5 V outputs therefore also selects 5 V input thresholds. It does not configure the motor power supply; a motor supply such as 48 V is a separate matter. The base hardware and motor component retain their existing 24 V I/O default; the position-output component applies its own selection afterwards. 323A:02 selects the shared input pull-up/pull-down.
Arm and disarm an output The runtime gate controls are:
   PV suffix Output-word bit Function     PosOut01-Ena 16 Output 1 gate   PosOut02-Ena 17 Output 2 gate   PosOut03-Ena 18 Output 3 gate    Each has a corresponding -RB readback. For example, substituting the actual slave prefix:
caput <prefix>PosOut01-Ena 0 caput <prefix>PosOut01-Ena 1 caget <prefix>PosOut01-Ena-RB These controls gate the configured position-derived signal. Enabling a gate does not command a single pulse or establish the pulse origin. Gate writes preserve other output bits, including the brake bit 0. The component uses bit-addressed WriteEcEntryEcPath; the records use asyn masks. Writing the complete BO01-Arr word replaces all bits and can change other gates.
The hardware snippet loads all six gate control/readback records directly, even when default substitutions are disabled. Output records use PINI=0/NO so initialization preserves the configured gates.
Separate software-PWM frequency test examples/PSI/lab_setup/N6/startup_software_pwm.cmd is an isolated bench candidate for fixed-frequency software PWM. It uses _OPT for masked output gates, loads no motion axis, and keeps the drive disabled with zero velocity. The test selects 5 V I/O and leaves the output gate disabled until explicitly armed. The companion README_software_pwm.md contains the scope procedure.
The reusable SDO configuration is now in ecmccomp. The startup applies:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyComponent.cmd "COMP=Drive-Generic-PWMOutput,CH_ID=1,MACROS='FREQUENCY_HZ=2000,DUTY_PERCENT=50,OUTPUT=1,PWM_ID=0,ARM=0,N6_IO_24V=0'"    Component macro Default Meaning     FREQUENCY_HZ 2000 Plain integer 50..2000 Hz   DUTY_PERCENT 50 Plain integer 0..100 percent; 0/100 give constant endpoints   OUTPUT 1 Physical output 1..3   PWM_ID 0 Generator 0 (3260, source 0x12) or 1 (3261, source 0x13)   ARM 0 Initial selected-output gate   N6_IO_24V 0 for first output; then inherit Shared voltage selection   N6_INPUT_PULLUP Inherit motor Shared input bias    Apply it after the motor and N6_OPT. Outputs sharing a PWM_ID must use the same frequency/duty. PositionOutput and PWMOutput may use different physical outputs on one drive, but cannot claim the same output or disagree on shared I/O settings. The motor cannot be reapplied after either output component. Generator 0 / output 1 / 2 kHz / 50% is the bench-reported case; other choices still require commissioning. No extra frequency/duty PVs are added.
The EtherCAT manual distinguishes a 2 kHz software-PWM limit from the 500 Hz limit for other output sources. PWM is a fixed-frequency signal, not a faster position-divider mode. A successful PWM measurement does not prove that the 100-full-step position output can exceed its documented limit. A PWM carrier gated by position is also not automatically phase-aligned to position or guaranteed to produce one pulse per compare point.
The candidate uses 3260:01=2000 Hz, 3260:02=50 percent and 3252:02=0x1210 (PWM 0 to output 1, gated by bit 16). Source 0x12 is explicitly listed in the newer N6 Modbus TCP manual v1.2.1 for FIR-v2542, section 7.1.2.3. The older EtherCAT v1.1.0 table omits that source despite listing the PWM parameter objects. The user subsequently reported the PWM test working on the EtherCAT drive on 2026-10-28. Numerical frequency/duty/jitter measurements were not supplied; this is evidence for that tested setup, not other variants.
Run the dedicated startup instead of the position-output startup, connect the scope to X4 pin 5 / GNDD pin 8, then arm PosOut01-Ena. Expected at 2 kHz/50%: a 500 microsecond full period with 250 microseconds high and low. Disarm after measurement. The test also accepts 500, 1000 and 1500 Hz by changing FREQUENCY_HZ in its component call and restarting. These are checkpoints, not the only supported integer frequencies. No extra PDOs, motor motion or drive-flash writes are needed. Restart the original 100-step startup to restore position routing. The output was reported working; exact frequency, duty and jitter still need recorded scope measurements.
No counter-clock input is documented for 3260; it provides frequency and duty parameters. Output routing selects PWM or position, and its gate is a 60FE:01 bit. A PLC may gate PWM over a position window, but this gives bursts of a time-based carrier rather than one edge per motor-step interval. It does not bypass the documented 500 Hz position-divider limit.
Drive homing method 35 Method 35 references the drive’s current position without a homing move. With home offset 0 it can establish the zero of logical position 6064, the source used for the periodic output. The manual explicitly states that raw 6063 is not zeroed by drive homing. Referencing the ecmc axis using an offset also leaves the drive counter unchanged and does not itself reference the drive-side output source.
The observed first-edge shift after method 35 is described below. Drive referencing and ecmc axis-coordinate referencing remain separate operations, coordinated by sequence 26 in the example.
PDOs and panel records With HOMING=1, the process image initializes homingMethod01=35 and homeOffset01=0. It also maps the drive homing dynamics, initialized to the manual’s presets: switch-search speed 50, zero-search speed 10 and acceleration 500. These are drive-defined user-unit values, separate from the YAML homing parameters used by ecmc. Method 35 makes no search move; configure and verify these values before using other drive homing methods. Mode remains CSV (9) until a sequence changes it.
   Entry Object/type Purpose     homingMethod01 6098:00, S8 Homing method; optional PDO   homeOffset01 607C:00, S32 Offset in configured 6064 units; optional PDO   homingVelocitySwitch01 6099:01, U32 Switch-search speed; initialized to 50   homingVelocityZero01 6099:02, U32 Zero/index-search speed; initialized to 10   homingAcceleration01 609A:00, U32 Drive homing acceleration; initialized to 500   modeControl01 6060:00, S8 Mode command: 6 homing, 9 CSV; already mapped   modeActual01 6061:00, S8 Mode acknowledgment; already mapped   driveControl01 6040:00, U16 Axis-owned controlword; already mapped   driveCmdExe01 B1 alias of 6040 bit 4 Sequence-26 trigger; present with HOMING=1   driveStatus01 6041:00, U16 Homing completion/error and drive status; already mapped    With the 100-full-step position unit, a home offset of 1 means 100 full steps (180 degrees on the tested motor), not one native encoder increment. Use offset 0 when referencing the current scaled position to zero.
Additional PVs are Drv01-HomeMethod, Drv01-HomeOffset and Drv01-ModeCmd, each with -RB, plus Drv01-ModeAct. Their command readbacks report the process-image command values; Drv01-ModeAct is the drive’s actual mode acknowledgment. Command records use PINI=0 so IOC initialization does not overwrite the initialized method, offset or mode. Additional command/readback pairs are Drv01-HomeVelTo, Drv01-HomeVelFrm and Drv01-HomeAcc, also with PINI=0. Edit them while the axis is idle. The EPICS edits use the nonnegative asynInt32 range; the mapped PDO type is U32.
Use axis homing sequence 26 The dedicated axis YAML now uses the existing drive-triggered homing sequence 26 (ECMC_SEQ_HOME_TRIGG_EXTERN), also used for SmarAct MCS2. No separate PLC or C++ homing state machine is required for the example.
axis: mode: CSV autoMode: modeSet: ec0.s$(DRV_SID).modeControl01 modeAct: ec0.s$(DRV_SID).modeActual01 modeCmdMotion: 9 modeCmdHome: 6 encoder: homing: type: 26 position: 0 trigg: ec0.s$(DRV_SID).driveCmdExe01.0 ready: ec0.s$(DRV_SID).driveStatus01.12 refAtHome: 1 timeout: 10 velocity: to: 18 from: 18 acceleration: 36 deceleration: 36 postMoveEnable: true postMovePosition: 0 This is an excerpt; retain the fine counter mapping and other axis settings from the complete example. The nonzero homing velocities/accelerations satisfy generic axis validation; drive method 35 makes no search move.
Sequence 26 switches to mode 6 and waits for the mode acknowledgment, asserts the trigger, waits for a rising edge on statusword bit 12, clears the trigger and references the ecmc encoder to position (zero here). The raw drive counter and Enc01-PosAct remain unchanged; the axis position gains its engineering offset. Normal axis enabling applies, so the motor may energize even though bare drive method 35 itself does not require Operation enabled.
The existing sequence restores mode 9 through its post-home stage. Therefore postMoveEnable is deliberately true, with postMovePosition equal to the home position. This waits for CSV mode acknowledgment and skips the move because the referenced position already equals the target. If these two positions are changed, keep them equal unless an actual post-home move is intended. The example uses a 10-second sequence timeout.
Trigger from the motor record After installing/restarting with RAW_POS=1,HOMING=1 and the dedicated YAML:
 Stop the axis and disable the output gate using PosOut01-Ena=0. Verify the Home tab shows method 35 and offset 0. Leave automatic mode switching to the axis; do not manually change mode while it is active. Use the normal M1 motor-record Home Forward or Home Reverse command. For method 35 the direction does not request a search move. The axis homing procedure is 26; this is distinct from drive method 35. Verify homing completes, the axis reads its configured home position, Drv01-ModeAct returns to 9 and Enc01-PosScaled shows the expected referenced drive position. Re-arm the output after checking the result.  For example, substituting the actual PV prefixes:
caput <slave-prefix>PosOut01-Ena 0 caput <axis-motor-record>.HOMF 1 # After successful homing and verification: caput <slave-prefix>PosOut01-Ena 1 The example’s motor record is named M1 under its configured IOC prefix. The output gate is not automatically coordinated with axis homing; these commands are separate. The hardware Home tab provides parameters and status; use the axis panel/motor record to start sequence 26.
On failure or timeout, stop/reset through the normal axis controls and verify the trigger is cleared and mode 9 is restored before resuming motion. Mode restoration after a successful home uses the post-home stage; do not assume an aborted sequence has completed that stage.
Why the trigger uses a separate bit alias The DS402 axis writes its full controlword every cycle. Sequence 26 writes its trigger earlier in the axis execution, so directly linking trigg to driveControl01.4 would let the later whole-word write clear it.
With HOMING=1, the snippet instead adds:
Cfg.EcAddDataDT(ec<master>.s<slave>.driveControl01,0,4,1,B1,driveCmdExe01) This follows the MCS2 approach. The B1 alias is initialized to zero and appended after the parent entry. During output-image transfer the parent controlword is written first; the alias then replaces only bit 4, preserving the other bits. Sequence 26 owns this alias and clears it when finished or stopped. The alias is not an additional PDO mapping.
Alternative PLC/C++ integration The inspected ecmc RT loop executes in this order:
Axis-local PLC → motion axis → C++ logic → normal global PLCs → EtherCAT send A normal global PLC can override an axis command after the axis executes; an axis-local PLC cannot reliably override the parent’s whole-word writes. However, with HOMING=1, the trigger alias is applied during output-image transfer after those writes. A custom PLC/C++ homing implementation must therefore write driveCmdExe01.0, not just driveControl01.4, and must not compete with sequence 26 for that alias. Coordinate mode, velocity, axis commands, timeout and output gates explicitly when replacing the built-in sequence. Do not run both trigger owners together.
The execution order and writes were checked in ecmcMainThread.cpp, ecmcDriveBase.cpp, ecmcAxisSequencer.cpp, ecmcEcSlave.cpp and ecmcEcData.cpp. Verify the behavior in the deployed ecmc version when using a custom override.
Repeatable first-edge shift after homing (2026-10-28) On the tested 100-full-step setup, a fresh start produced the first output edge after 100 full steps. After method-35 homing, the first edge was observed after 50 full steps, followed by transitions after another 100 steps: 50, 150, 250, … full steps of subsequent motion. This behavior was repeatable. The scaled position was reported to return to zero on homing.
The observation is a shift of the first-edge position; the following edge spacing remains 100 full steps. Here “edge” means an output state change, not a complete high/low pulse cycle. For the tested 200-step motor, 50 steps are 90 degrees and 100 steps are 180 degrees.
Homing once after startup, before beginning a measurement, is therefore a proposed way to obtain a consistent first edge after 50 full steps. The example does not automatically home at startup: command the normal M1 home sequence, verify completion and CSV restoration, then begin the measurement. Coordinate the output gate as described above. This proposal uses the reported repeatability; it does not establish behavior for other firmware, intervals, directions or restart conditions.
Homing checks still needed on the drive Sequence 26 detects a rising edge on the configured ready bit. Verify first and repeated method-35 requests: statusword bit 12 may already be high from a previous home, and a fast operation must still produce an observable completion transition. The sequence has no separate configured input for homing-error bit 13; monitor it in the Home tab and verify timeout/error behavior. Also check statusword bit 10, trigger clearing, mode restoration and first-edge behavior under other motion/restart conditions. The repeatable 100-step/50-step first-edge observation above does not establish all these cases. These are hardware commissioning checks, not outcomes established by the configuration tests.
Records and panels    PV suffix Meaning     Enc01-PosAct Fine 6063 counter with RAW_POS=1; otherwise legacy 6064   Enc01-PosScaled Scaled 6064; present with RAW_POS=1   PosOut01-Ena through PosOut03-Ena Individual output gates, each with -RB   CfgRawPosition Resolved raw-position option, read-only   CfgHoming Resolved homing option, read-only   CfgCapture Resolved capture option, read-only   CfgAnalogIn Resolved analog input option, read-only   BO01-Arr Complete output word, including the brake and output gates    The hardware selects ecmcN6-1-1-1-S_OPT.ui and ecmcN6-1-1-1-S_OPT_expert.ui. The usual position field shows fine feedback with RAW_POS=1; the additional scaled field is visible with CfgRawPosition=1. Counter readouts use integer precision.
Both displays have a Home tab. CfgHoming=1 reveals its homing fields; otherwise it reports that the PDOs are not mapped. The compact tab shows method, offset and actual mode readbacks. The expert tab adds editable parameters/mode, command readbacks and statusword bits 10, 12 and 13. The expert display also retains the output gate controls and readbacks. The Home tab separates Mode and Speed fields; Speed shows the new drive homing dynamics (editable in Expert, read-only in the compact display). Capture and Analog tabs expose their optional readbacks only when CfgCapture=1 / CfgAnalogIn=1. Capture has Home, In 3 and In 4 sub-tabs; its control fields are readbacks, not writable arming controls. The original panels remain available for the base descriptor.
After installing updated files, restart the IOC to load new records and reopen the panel to load its new layout. Changing the panel alone does not add missing IOC records.
Commissioning evidence and troubleshooting The bench measurements support using raw 6063 as the fine open-loop counter on FIR-v2542-B1080909 with 60E6:01=0. One approximate revolution changed 6063 by 3,270,300 counts (about 359.29 degrees at the nominal scale) and 6064 by two counts. The fine-counter axis and the 100-step output were then reported working together.
The manual warns that 6063 values are invalid when the interface resolution is zero. The observed open-loop behavior is therefore specific evidence for this firmware/setup, not a guarantee for other firmware, motor modes or sensors. Hardware-free checks cover mapping, component validation, record links, gate masks and panel compilation/visibility; they do not establish the drive’s waveform or homing behavior.
Earlier pulse-generator attempts The initial 205C pulse-generator approach tried to retain native 6064 units. At 16,384 increments/full step, 100 full steps require a divider of 1,638,400, which does not fit the documented 16-bit ratio. A trial with one pulse per full step still failed when selecting the pulse-generator source: 3203:01=8 repeatedly aborted with 0x06040047 (internal incompatibility).
Enabling nominal sensorless resolution with 60E6:01=3276800 subsequently produced drive error 7305h (sensor 1 faulty). The working configuration keeps 60E6:01=0, leaves feedback selection unchanged and writes neither 3203 nor 205C. The earlier pulse-generator example files are failed prototypes, not the recommended configuration.
Useful readbacks For the lab master 1, slave 0; adjust these addresses for another setup:
ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type string 0x100A 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x6041 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x603F 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint32 0x60E6 1 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint32 0x60A8 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type uint16 0x3252 2 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type int32 0x6063 0 ethercat upload -m1 -p0 --type int32 0x6064 0 For the 100-step/output-1 setup, expect 60E6:01=0, 60A8=0x02AC0000 and 3252:02=0x0910. Sequential SDO uploads are not a simultaneous position sample; stop motion when comparing paired readings.
6041 bit 3 identifies an active drive fault. 603F reports the last error and may retain 7305 after its cause has gone. Reset a latched fault using the normal drive controls once the cause is resolved. An SDO controlword write while the axis owns the cyclic PDO will be overwritten.
For blank gate or homing fields, check record existence in the IOC shell:
dbgrep *PosOut* dbgrep *CfgHoming* dbgrep *HomeMethod* There should be three gate controls and three gate readbacks. Homing parameter records are present only with HOMING=1; capture and analog records similarly require their options. Missing records require updating the loaded configuration/database files and restarting the IOC.
Sources and related configuration  Nanotec N6 EtherCAT technical manual, FIR-v2508, version 1.1.0: method 35 in section 6.4.2.11; object entries 6063, 607C, 6098, 323A and 3252. Base N6 configuration. ecmc homing sequences. examples/PSI/lab_setup/N6/README_position_output_100_steps.md: lab setup and commissioning notes. ecmccomp docs/N6_position_output.md: component interface and constraints.  Ownership of the N6 configuration snippets Reusable SDO setup belongs in ecmccomp. Hardware PDOs, records and panels remain in ecmccfg, and examples choose components and parameter values.

The failed trial and its broad recovery are deliberately not packaged as reusable components.

title: legacy motion
content:
Scope This page covers the older classic motion configuration flow that is still used in many existing IOCs and in the examples/ESS/ tree.
For new configurations, prefer the YAML-based workflow with loadYamlAxis.cmd. The legacy flow is mainly relevant when:
 maintaining an existing IOC based on .ax, .vax, and .sax files reading or reusing older ESS examples migrating a classic configuration step by step instead of rewriting everything at once  Main legacy entry points  configureAxis.cmd configure one physical axis from a classic axis file configureVirtualAxis.cmd configure one virtual axis from a classic virtual-axis file applyAxisSynchronization.cmd apply synchronization logic from a classic sync file configureSlave.cmd older combined slave setup path applySlaveConfig.cmd apply a predefined slave configuration  Classic file types  .ax physical axis configuration .vax virtual axis configuration .sax synchronization between axes, often used for slit, mirror, or simple gear structures  Typical startup pattern:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}configureAxis.cmd, "CONFIG=./cfg/linear_1.ax" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}configureVirtualAxis.cmd, "CONFIG=./cfg/center.vax" ${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}applyAxisSynchronization.cmd, "CONFIG=./cfg/center.sax" ESS examples that use this flow The examples/ESS/ tree is the main reference for classic motion startup. Typical patterns there include:
 standalone physical axes with configureAxis.cmd slit and mirror structures using .ax + .vax + .sax simple gear and synchronization examples using applyAxisSynchronization.cmd older combined slave setup with configureSlave.cmd and applySlaveConfig.cmd  Representative examples:
 examples/ESS/mcu1025.script examples/ESS/mcu1024_slit/mcu1024.script examples/ESS/mcu1025_slit/mcu1025.script examples/ESS/mcu1021_coupler_simplegear/mcu1021_coupler.script examples/ESS/mcu1025_slitdemo/mcu1025.script  Relationship to the current YAML flow The current preferred workflow is:
 slave setup with addSlave.cmd and applyComponent.cmd axis setup with loadYamlAxis.cmd PLC setup with loadYamlPlc.cmd or loadPLCFile.cmd  The legacy motion flow is still valid, but compared to YAML it has these limitations:
 less structured validation less consistency between physical axes, virtual axes, and synchronization harder reuse across projects  Practical migration advice When updating an older IOC, do not try to migrate everything at once.
A practical order is:
 keep the existing classic motion files running unchanged replace old slave-specific setup with applyComponent.cmd where possible migrate one axis at a time from .ax to YAML migrate virtual/synchronized structures after the physical axes are stable  If the IOC is stable and there is no strong need for migration, it is often better to keep the classic motion part as-is and only document that it is a legacy configuration.

Axis diagnostic text <prefix><axis>-IlockShrtTxt, <prefix><axis>-IlockTxt, and <prefix><axis>-MsgTxt are loaded with ecmcRtLogAxis.db, independently of motor records. Their names are unchanged; they use RTLOG_AXIS_ILOCK_SHORT_TEXT, RTLOG_AXIS_ILOCK_TEXT, and RTLOG_AXIS_MESSAGE_TEXT on ${ECMC_RTLOG_PORT=ecmcRTLog}, addressed by the ECMC axis number.
IlockShrtTxt preserves the existing last-interlock abbreviations. When no interlock is reported, it can show an ignored motion request, for example IgnAbs. The short labels are IgnAbs, IgnRel, IgnVel, IgnHome, and IgnPVT. IlockTxt gives the corresponding explanation, for example Ignored ABS: positioning disabled. Both fields prioritize interlocks. This is display information only and sets no interlock or error. The ignored indication clears when that permission is restored, silent-ignore mode is switched off, or a new motion starts. The diagnostic report and JSON dump retain the ignored-request count and last ignored command until IOC restart.
MsgTxt shows native ECMC errors first, then native warnings, and otherwise motor-driver messages when motor support is present. Native messages and interlocks continue to update with the amplifier disabled or without motor support. These remain EPICS string records (39 visible characters). All three text PVs use the diagnostic port; the full explanations fit within the EPICS string length.
Upgrade the ECMC module and configuration databases together and restart the IOC. Custom motor templates must remove their old definitions of these three PVs to avoid duplicate records. Standalone custom configurations must load ecmcRtLogAxis.db for each axis.

title: Motor record examples
content:
This page contains example-specific configurations and test results. For general motor-record behavior, see Motor Record. For restore options, startup ordering, and soft-limit precedence, use Motor position and soft-limit autosave.
Topics  Auto-save restore Open loop stepper with retries No motor record  Auto-save restore Test IOC for open loop stepper motor with auto-save-restore The example is based on that PSI ioc install tool is used.
Auto save restore configurations Auto save/restore of motor position is made through motor record. At PSI if the tool “ioc install” is used, its enough to add a file <ioc_name>_pos.req in the “./cfg/” sub dir listing the DVAL field of the motor record names that need to be auto saved restored.
In order for restore of motor position to succeed, both autosave restore passes, 0 and 1, must execute before iocInit. The PSI directive #ENABLE-PASS=2 selects two passes; 2 is not a pass number.
NOTE: The position-restore example uses an incremental encoder (encoder.type: 0). Soft-limit restoration is independent of position restoration; see autosave.
Example of a _pos.req file in ./cfg/ ioc install automatically adds restore at both passes ("#ENABLE-PASS=2") if filename ends with “_pos.req”
MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DVAL Example of a x.req file in ./cfg/ If the file is named something else (without ending with “_pos.req”) then also “#ENABLE-PASS=2” needs to be added:
#ENABLE-PASS=2 MTEST04-MTN-ASM:Axis1.DVAL Open loop stepper with retries The motion axis in this example is configured to move in open loop but executing retries based on an absolute encoder.
General configuration Two encoders are configured for the motion object:
 01: BISS-C absolute encoder 02: Open loop counter  The system will startup with the open loop encoder as primary (used for control) and the motor record are configured to use retries to control on the absolute BISS-C encoder.
Motor record Important motor record fields are:
 RTRY : Max retry count RMOD : Retry Mode UEIP : Use encoder if present RDBD : Retry deadband URIP : Use RDBL Link If Present RDBL : Readback link (position from an EPICS variable)  RTRY : Max retry count maximum retry count. Needs to be set to a number higher than 0
RMOD : Retry Mode Can be set to:
 0: “Unity” 1: “Arithmetic” 2: “Geometric” 3: “In-Position”  Use setting 1 or 2 for this test, for more information read motor record doc.
UEIP : Use encoder if present Not used in this test. Set to 0.
RDBD : Retry deadband Set to 0.01mm in this test (motor record will execute new mode if outside this limit).
URIP : Use RDBL Link If Present Set to 1
RDBL : Readback link (position from EPICS variable) This should be a record holding the value for control, could any PV. In this example another configured encoder is used
In this example the axis encoder 01 <prefix>:<axis_name>-Enc<enc_id>-PosAct
Feed settings to motor record by epics.motorRecord.fieldInit var: Any vars added to epics.motorRecord.fieldInit will be forwarded to motor record at init:
##### Pass extra parameters to motor record: # RTRY : Max retry count # RMOD : Retry Mode # UEIP : Use encoder if present # RDBD : Retry deadband # URIP : Use RDBL Link If Present # RDBL : Readback link (position from an EPICS variable) epics: name: ${AX_NAME=M1} # Axis name precision: 3 # Decimal count description: Test cfg # Axis description unit: mm # Unit motorRecord: syncSoftLimits: False fieldInit: 'FOFF=Frozen,RRES=1.0,RTRY=2,RMOD=1,UEIP=0,RDBD=0.1,URIP=1,RDBL=$(IOC):${AX_NAME=M1}-Enc${RTRY_ENC_CH=01}-PosAct' NOTE: Do not use “CP” on the RDBL link…
Running the test  Start:  iocsh.bash startup.cmd Run positioning commands:  dbpf IOC_TEST:Axis1 10 Now the motion should be going stepwise (depending on RTRY) and end up in:
 ecmc act pos = 10/0.95 motor record act pos = 10  NOTE: JOGGING is not supported (motor record will stop any started JOGGING cmd)
Stop on RDBL pv alarms Motor record stops motion if the RDBL linked PV is in alarm state (MAJOR or INVALID) independent on if severity propagation is set (disregarding NMS,MS,MSS…)
The simulated position is configured like this:
 field(LOW, "-50") field(LOLO, "-60") field(HIGH, "50") field(HIHI, "60") IMPORTANT: If you use an incremental encoder linked to calc record, you can sometimes experience stops during homing sequence since then the motion axis might go outside of the alarm limits defined. Normally motor record driver will not update the position during homing but I will happen for instance when activating limit switch or homing switch. Then a stop could occur This is of course no problem if the RDBL linked value is absolute like intended.
How to move when RDBL alarm interlock If motion is interlocked by the RDBL alarm then motion can be executed by setting the URIP to 0 (disabling RDBL).
dbpf IOC_TEST:Axis1.URIP 0 Motion can now be executed. Note: The RDBL link are now not used (retries based on RDBL will not be executed)
No motor record In yaml configuration use epics.motorRecord.enable = False:
epics: name: ${AX_NAME=M1} # Axis name precision: 3 # Decimal count description: Test cfg # Axis description unit: mm # Unit motorRecord: enable: False
