title: Drive output lookup-table compensation
content:
Purpose A CSV axis can add a position-dependent feed-forward value to its drive output. This is useful for a voice coil working against a spring, gravity compensation, or another repeatable load that needs a non-zero command to remain stationary.
The compensation is applied as:
raw drive output = (controller output + scale * LUT(actual position)) / drive scale + raw drive offset Both LUT columns use engineering units:
 column 1: actual axis position, in the encoder/axis position unit column 2: CSV drive-command offset, in the controller-output unit  The sum passes through the normal drive.numerator and drive.denominator scaling. Do not store raw EtherCAT setpoint counts in the LUT.
This feature affects CSV velocity/force output only. It does not alter CSP position output. Drive interlocks suppress the compensation.
YAML configuration axis: mode: CSV drive: numerator: 1 denominator: 1000 lookuptable: filename: ./cfg/voice_coil_spring.lut scale: 1.0 enable: true # range: 360.0 # optional modulo range in position engineering units Loading a valid table enables it by default. Set enable: false when the table should be loaded but not active. scale defaults to 1.0; use -1.0 to invert the compensation sign. If range is positive, the actual position is wrapped into 0 <= position < range before lookup.
LUT file # position [mm] holding output [engineering units] -10.0 -0.80 0.0 0.00 10.0 0.85 Values between rows are interpolated by the standard ecmc lookup-table implementation. Outside the table domain, the closest endpoint is used.
Direct commands Cfg.LoadAxisDrvLookupTable(1,./cfg/voice_coil_spring.lut) Cfg.SetAxisDrvLookupTableScale(1,1.0) Cfg.SetAxisDrvLookupTableRange(1,0) Cfg.SetAxisDrvLookupTableEnable(1,1) The corresponding query commands are GetAxisDrvLookupTableEnable, GetAxisDrvLookupTableScale, and GetAxisDrvLookupTableRange. GetAxisDrvLookupTableValue(axis) returns the compensation applied in the last drive cycle, after LUT scaling but before normal drive scaling, in CSV drive-command engineering units. It returns zero when compensation is disabled, interlocked, or not applicable.
Commission the LUT initially with conservative drive limits and verify its sign over the full travel before relying on it for holding force.

title: Encoder relay power control
content:
Encoder relay power control reduces the time an absolute encoder, such as a BiSS encoder in vacuum, is powered. It is disabled by default and configured separately for each encoder. Existing axes keep their previous behavior.
Power-off and wake-up After a move completes, the encoder stays powered until the axis has remained atTarget for the configured power-off delay. When a positive controller deadband is smaller than the atTarget tolerance, the axis must also be within that deadband. Losing either condition resets the delay. atTarget monitoring must be enabled with a positive tolerance; otherwise the configuration is rejected.
The encoder can power off while the amplifier remains enabled and holds torque. ECMC suspends its feedback correction while feedback is unavailable: CSV velocity output is zero and CSP holds its position setpoint without ECMC outer-loop correction. Drive auto-disable remains independent. If the drive disables first, encoder power is removed after drive-enabled feedback goes low.
While encoder power is off, position is stale and physical drift cannot be detected. Use this mode only where the drive and mechanics can hold position without that encoder, for example an appropriate stepper setup. A drive’s own internal feedback loop must remain functional. Do not power off feedback that the drive itself needs for commutation or position holding.
Every new motion request wakes the encoder, including when the drive is already enabled and drive auto-enable is disabled. ECMC waits for the power-up delay and for the ready input, if linked. Without a ready input, the configured delay is used. Two consecutive valid RT cycles qualify readiness, and a fresh absolute sample is acquired before motion starts. Relative moves use that fresh position. STOP cancels a pending move; a wake-up timeout faults the axis and disables it.
Intentionally unpowered or warming encoders do not raise not-ready or encoder hardware alarms during idle/startup. Once ready, loss of readiness or an encoder alarm is a fault. Transport and relay-output errors are not treated as normal idle conditions.
Initial startup read On initial runtime startup, ECMC powers every encoder configured for relay power control once, even when the tracking counter is selected. Power-up starts when EtherCAT process data is valid. Axis startup waits for the configured minimum warm-up delay, optional ready input and a valid position sample. The existing startupDelay and startupTimeout settings apply; no additional setting or asyn parameter is required. A missing ready signal times out and faults the axis without enabling the drive. A successful read does not command a move or change autoEnable.atStartup.
Normal automatic power management resumes after startup. With a configured backup, the settled source is referenced into the counter before power-off, using the configured idle delay. The initial absolute coordinate remains available as the retained readback while the source is off.
This read does not zero or calibrate the absolute encoder. Configure the correct absolute offset or explicitly reference the encoder with the drive disabled. An absolute coordinate outside the machine’s configured travel window may therefore expose invalid derived virtual-axis limits during startup instead of on the first move. Correct that coordinate reference before accepting motion; do not suppress these errors as part of the power check.
Configure an encoder This first implementation supports absolute encoders. Incremental encoders are rejected because cycling power can lose their reference. Configure the relay after loading the axis/encoder YAML, before starting runtime. The encoder.power YAML group below works with both Python/Jinja and ECB. Native startup commands remain available for existing configurations.
Example for encoder 2 on axis 6; replace the output entry with the actual relay:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SelectAxisEncConfig(6,2)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.LinkEcEntryToObject(ec0.s5.binaryOutput03,ax6.enc.power)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisMonEnableAtTargetMon(6,1)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisMonAtTargetTol(6,0.01)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrPol(6,1)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrDelay(6,0.1)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrTimeout(6,5)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrOffDelay(6,2)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrEnable(6,1)"    Setting Meaning Default     SetAxisEncPwrEnable(axis,enable) Enable relay power control 0   SetAxisEncPwrPol(axis,activeHigh) Output 1 powers encoder when 1; output 0 when 0 1   SetAxisEncPwrDelay(axis,seconds) Minimum power-up delay, including with ready input 0.1 s   SetAxisEncPwrTimeout(axis,seconds) Maximum time allowed for wake-up 5 s   SetAxisEncPwrOffDelay(axis,seconds) Continuous settling time after atTarget 2 s    Delays must be finite and nonnegative; the wake-up timeout must be greater than the power-up delay. Configure with the axis disabled and encoder power off. Output polarity and ready-input polarity are independent. Link ax6.enc.ready as usual and use Cfg.SetAxisEncInvHwReady(6,1) for an active-low ready input. All encoder settings act on the selected configuration encoder, not automatically on the primary encoder. Each power-controlled encoder must be ready before the axis can start. Restore the desired configuration-encoder selection afterward.
Idle power-off is supported for internal trajectories. External trajectories must retain powered feedback; switching to an external trajectory while an encoder is off requires waking it first.
Readback and errors PREFIX:AXIS-Enc02-PwrState reports encoder 2’s power state decoded from bits 8…10 of ax6.enc.status2. Each encoder has one general status-word asyn parameter, with additional flags for readiness, homed and absolute type.
   Value State     0 Ordinary mode: ECMC does not control a relay   1 Intentionally powered off; position is stale   2 Warming up; motion waits   3 Ready; valid feedback available   4 Fault    GetAxisEncPwrState(axis) and the matching GetAxisEncPwrEnable, GetAxisEncPwrPol, GetAxisEncPwrDelay, GetAxisEncPwrTimeout, and GetAxisEncPwrOffDelay queries read the selected configuration encoder.
ERROR_ENC_POWER_TIMEOUT (0x1441d) indicates wake-up timed out. ERROR_ENC_POWER_CONFIG (0x1441e) indicates invalid power-control settings. Normal powered-off and warming states do not produce a power-state alarm; Fault is a major alarm. An error reset is required after a power fault.
Slit simulation tests The dedicated slit_matrix_sim_test fixture (schema 3) links EL2008 outputs 03 and 04 to the LO and HI EL5042 supply relays. The encoder_power test group opts into supply simulation, publishing EL5042 raw position zero and ready low while unpowered. The drive counter and mechanics retain their physical position.
From the ECMC repository, with the updated IOC running:
python3 tests/integration/slit/run.py --prefix SIMSLIT: --run --case encoder_power Twelve cases run in each loop mode; three feedback-change cases are skipped in open loop. Coverage includes active-high/low relay outputs, short/long idle power-off delays, minimum startup delay versus early/late ready, motor and native requests, relative wake with the amplifier still enabled, timeout and STOP cancellation. Deterministic measurement disturbances check that atTarget loss or a tighter controller deadband prevents premature power-off. Once the feedback settles, the encoder must remain powered for the configured dwell.
These cases temporarily select the mode and restore ordinary feedback, native settings and encoder selection during cleanup. Restart the IOC with the updated fixture before running them. CA observations allow publication latency; exact RT-cycle timers are also tested by ECMC’s standalone encoder-power tests.
Off-state rollover coverage alternates zero and an all-ones raw counter word. The test verifies that the injected jump exceeds ECMC’s rollover threshold, checks retained encoder position while off, and repeats relative moves after wake-up without rehoming or resetting between cycles. Standalone production tests also cover a valid sample near the upper counter boundary, operation without a ready input, and preservation of already accumulated positive and negative turns across power cycles.
The wake-position-jump case injects positive and negative EL5042 measurement steps while encoder power is off, each exceeding five atTarget tolerances. Retained feedback must stay unchanged until wake-up. Relative motion must then use the fresh shifted position, without adding physical travel to compensate for the measurement step. The case requires closed-loop EL5042 feedback and leaves the following-error monitor enabled.
python3 tests/integration/slit/run.py --prefix SIMSLIT: --run --case encoder_power --test wake_position_jump --loop closed Counter handover mode For a linear stepper/absolute-encoder axis, an optional handover mode keeps control connected to an always-powered incremental counter while the absolute encoder is off. It complements the original power mode. Select it explicitly; backup index zero retains the original behavior. This first version supports CSV real axes and virtual test axes, internal encoder feedback, and no modulo range. The counter must not have encoder power control enabled.
When the completed move has satisfied atTarget, any tighter controller deadband, and the encoder idle delay, ECMC references the counter to the absolute position and copies its Homed state. It selects counter feedback before removing absolute encoder power. Counter position remains live and the CSV controller continues using it while the absolute encoder is off or warming. Manual primary selection is blocked while handover owns that selection. The usual primary-encoder PV shows the currently selected encoder.
A new request restores absolute power and waits for its configured delay and ready input, if linked. Before selecting it again, ECMC compares the fresh absolute position to the referenced counter. A discrepancy above the configured limit raises ERROR_ENC_POWER_MISMATCH (0x1441f), disables the axis and cancels the pending move. Counter feedback remains selected. Reset alone does not replay the rejected move; a new request is required. Within the limit, ECMC switches feedback and rebases the trajectory/controller before releasing the move. REL commands use the fresh absolute coordinate.
The initial startup read establishes the absolute coordinate; the counter has not yet been referenced to it, so a mismatch comparison is not available until the first completed handover. Motion remains blocked until absolute feedback is valid. This is not an absolute-position plausibility check at boot.
In this new mode, a normal drive disable does not shorten the encoder’s settling delay. Faults and explicit cancellation still abort pending motion. A counter cannot detect missed steps or external mechanical movement that it does not measure; the wake comparison detects disagreement before motion resumes.
Configure with the axis stopped/disabled and the absolute encoder powered off. After the usual relay/delay setup, for absolute encoder 2 and counter 1:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SelectAxisEncConfig(6,2)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrEnable(6,1)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrBackup(6,1,0.02)" The selected configuration encoder supplies the absolute feedback. Backup indices are one-based; the final argument is the positive, finite mismatch limit in axis engineering units. There is one handover pair per axis. GetAxisEncPwrSource(6), GetAxisEncPwrBackup(6) and GetAxisEncPwrDiffTol(6) report the configured pair and tolerance. Source and backup queries return zero when handover is disabled.
Disable handover with Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrBackup(6,0,0.02) while stopped/disabled. This leaves the current feedback selection in place. Before manually selecting the absolute encoder, restore its power and valid feedback. Disable handover before disabling encoder power control itself.
The existing schema-3 slit fixture already has both encoders and the relay links. Rebuild/install ECMC and restart the IOC to use the new commands, then:
python3 tests/integration/slit/run.py --prefix SIMSLIT: --run --case encoder_handover --loop closed This group checks repeated counter/absolute handover, positive and negative wake mismatches, cancellation without replay, and missing-ready timeout. All seven cases skip in open-loop mode, where the normal fixture already uses the counter as primary. No additional fixture links are required.
Generic operator selection and inspection power The axis does not infer an encoder’s hardware role from its index. The operator selector is Auto power, Encoder 1, … Encoder 8. Only indices configured on that axis are accepted. In the slit example encoder 1 happens to be the counter and encoder 2 the absolute encoder; another axis can assign them differently.
   Mode value Behavior     0: Auto power Default. Uses the configured relay policy and optional source/backup pair. Without either feature configured, existing axis behavior is unchanged.   1…8: Encoder N Fixed control feedback from that configured encoder. Keeps its own reference; selecting it does not reference or home either encoder. A power-controlled selected encoder stays powered and must finish its delay/readiness checks before selection and motion. Unselected encoders are not automatically powered by moves.    Changing mode requires a stopped, disabled axis with no pending motion. The initial implementation supports internal encoder feedback and CSV real axes (or virtual test axes). The fixed selector also works without a handover pair. It does not assume BiSS, EL5042, or open-loop hardware. The automatic power pair still requires the absolute source and always-powered incremental backup specified in its configuration.
The Enc tab in ecmcAxisExpert.ui provides the mode selector, accepted mode, active feedback index and power states for the configured encoders. The dedicated encoder panels provide the per-encoder inspection hold. The expert panel retains its existing dimensions.
Use PREFIX:AXIS-EncMode and -EncMode-RB for requested/accepted mode. The existing -SetEncIdCmd-RB shows the encoder actually controlling the axis. Mode acceptance can precede selection while a powered encoder warms up. No mode change enables the drive or executes motion. Returning from fixed powered feedback to Auto starts a fresh atTarget/deadband dwell before power-off in handover mode.
For inspection, PREFIX:AXIS-Enc02-ForceOn=1 holds encoder 2 powered until explicitly released. Use the corresponding encoder number for other encoders. It must have power control configured. The hold does not change feedback selection or start motion and remains set after completed moves. Its accepted value is published through -Enc02-ForceOn-RB. Releasing it (0) restarts the qualified settling delay; a fixed selected powered encoder remains powered. Fault handling takes precedence. Use this control rather than the relay PDO.
The native command equivalents are:
ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncMode(6,1)" ecmcConfig "GetAxisEncMode(6)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrCtrl(6,1)" ecmcConfig "GetAxisEncPwrCtrl(6)" # Release inspection power and return to the configured automatic policy: ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncPwrCtrl(6,0)" ecmcConfigOrDie "Cfg.SetAxisEncMode(6,0)" Mode selection continues to use the existing axis words. Every encoder now has one shared UInt32Digital control parameter, including encoders without probe/latch configuration. Probe commands and power hold use masked bits of that same parameter; no separate Force ON asyn parameter is allocated.
   Word Bits Mask Meaning     axN.control 14…17 0x0003c000 Auto power=0, fixed encoder=1…8   axN.status 25…28 0x1e000000 Accepted mode   axN.enc.controlM 0 0x1 Probe/latch enable   axN.enc.controlM 1 0x2 Probe/latch arm   axN.enc.controlM 2 0x4 Automatic rearm   axN.enc.controlM 3 0x8 Force encoder M power ON; command and readback    Axis control bit 18 and status bit 29 are retired. Writes with axis bit 18 set are rejected. Replace the old axis -EncForceOn PV with the explicit per-encoder -EncNN-ForceOn PV and rebuild ECMC/restart the IOC with matching databases. The native SetAxisEncPwrCtrl command remains available for the configured automatic power source (or primary encoder when no source is configured); the per-encoder PV does not change the configuration index.
Both words remain 32 bits. Existing control bits 0…13, status bits 0…24, and the sequence/interlock word retain their layout. Writes to control fields must be masked to preserve unrelated commands.
The encoder_handover simulation group includes fixed Encoder 1/2 selection through both EPICS and native text commands, plus inspection power that retains counter feedback and survives a completed move. Rebuild/install ECMC and ecmccfg and restart the dedicated test IOC before running the new controls.
Encoder status word Each encoder publishes one read-only 32-bit axN.enc.statusM asyn parameter through an Int32 interface. It replaces the dedicated enc.powerstateM parameter; both are not allocated. The encoder status is independent of the axis status/control words.
   Bit(s) Mask Meaning     0 0x00000001 Encoder relay power control enabled   1 0x00000002 Relay power commanded ON (logical state, independent of output polarity)   2 0x00000004 Feedback ready: initialized, valid transport and no current encoder error; powered feedback has completed warm-up/readiness checks   3 0x00000008 Encoder homed/referenced   4 0x00000010 Configured absolute encoder type; clear for incremental   8…10 0x00000700 Power state: 0 Ordinary, 1 Off, 2 Warming, 3 Ready, 4 Fault    Other bits are reserved and zero. The power-command bit reports ECMC’s logical relay command, not a measurement of supply voltage. With power control disabled, it is clear even if the hardware has an independent, continuously powered supply. Homed and absolute describe the encoder object and remain visible while its supply is intentionally off; they do not imply that a fresh position is available.
For example, encoder 2 exposes:
 PREFIX:AXIS-Enc02-Stat: complete status word. -Enc02-PwrEnable-RB, -Enc02-PwrOn, -Enc02-Ready: individual power/readiness bits. -Enc02-Homed, -Enc02-Absolute: reference and encoder-type bits. -Enc02-PwrState: existing five-state display, decoded from bits 8…10.  All derived records use a single native Int32 status reader, so homed, absolute and power readbacks require no extra asyn parameters. The existing expert-panel power-state displays keep their PV names. Deploy matching ECMC and ecmccfg updates and restart the IOC because the native parameter name has changed.
The dedicated ecmcAxisEncExpert.ui encoder panel shows bits 0…4 as labelled indicators in its Status bits section, with the full word in hexadecimal. Hover an indicator for its meaning. Encoder selection uses the existing ENC_ID macro; panel dimensions and existing controls are preserved.
YAML configuration: Python/Jinja and ECB Both parsers accept encoder.power on the axis’s initial encoder or in a separate encoder YAML loaded with loadYamlEnc.cmd. Put the group on the encoder whose supply is switched; its index becomes the handover source. The optional backup index identifies an always-powered incremental encoder. The backup may be configured later during startup. No hardware type is inferred from an index.
For example, in the YAML loaded as encoder 2, after configuring counter 1 and positive, enabled axis atTarget monitoring:
encoder: # Existing absolute encoder position, scaling, ready and primary settings... type: 1 power: enable: true output: ec0.s2.BO05.0 activeHigh: true startupDelay: 0.1 startupTimeout: 5.0 idleDelay: 2.0 backup: encoder: 1 maxPositionDifference: 0.02    Key under encoder.power Meaning Default     enable Enable automatic relay power control false   output Full writable EtherCAT bit path, required when enabled none   activeHigh Logical ON writes 1 when true, 0 when false true   startupDelay Minimum warm-up time in seconds, including when ready is linked 0.1   startupTimeout Maximum wake time in seconds; must exceed startupDelay 5.0   idleDelay Continuous settled atTarget/tighter-deadband time before power-off, seconds 2.0   backup.encoder Tracking encoder index, 1…8; must differ from source none   backup.maxPositionDifference Positive permitted source/backup discrepancy on wake, engineering units none    Omitting power generates no power commands. An empty group or enable: false selects ordinary operation. With enable: false, a supplied output still links the relay to that encoder, without enabling automatic power control. Timing, polarity and backup settings are applied only when enabling the mode. This lets a test fixture declare its wiring in YAML and opt into power control at runtime. Omitting backup retains power control without automatic feedback handover. Use YAML booleans true/false, and finite, nonnegative delays. The existing encoder.ready input remains optional. Existing monitoring.target and controller deadband settings supply the settling criteria; the new group does not silently enable or change these monitors.
The shared template emits power setup after monitoring in an axis file, or after encoder creation in an additional encoder file. It clears the initial delay before setting the requested timeout, so a valid timeout shorter than the default 0.1-second delay also works. Both schemas reject invalid types, negative delays, out-of-range backup indices and incomplete backup settings. Cross-field guards emit a diagnostic and ecmcExit for a missing enabled output, a non-absolute or external-feedback source, an invalid timeout/delay relation, or zero discrepancy tolerance. Native validation also rejects missing/disabled atTarget monitoring, invalid links, a nonexistent/self/unsuitable backup, CSP handover and modulo axes.
Encoder files may be loaded in either order. Final axis validation checks that both encoders exist and have suitable types, power settings and drive mode before runtime starts. Runtime mapping changes require a complete valid pair and a stopped, disabled axis, with the source not ready. There is one handover pair per axis. Startup remains in Auto power mode; fixed encoder selection and the inspection Force ON hold are operator controls, not YAML keys. Deploy the updated ecmccfg templates/schema files. Order-independent startup requires ECMC with deferred encoder-pair validation; rebuild/install ECMC and restart the IOC when upgrading from the earlier implementation.

title: Examples
content:
How to use this page Prefer examples/PSI/best_practice/ as the public, reusable starting point for new configurations. Pick the example that is closest to your hardware or use case, copy it into your IOC area, and then adapt the macros, component selection, and YAML files.
Start from these first  I want a minimal axis example: Quickstart I want stepper motion with common Beckhoff terminals: Stepper BiSS-C I want incremental stepper examples: EL7047 + EL5102 or EX7062 CSV or EL7062 CSP I want PLC examples: basic PLCs or master-less PLC I want data storage: data storage buffer  Motion examples  Stepper BiSS-C EL7041/EL5042 and EL7062/EL5042 examples Stepper incremental, EL7047 + EL5102 Stepper incremental, EX7062 CSV Stepper incremental, EL7062 CSP SmarAct MCS2 PVT profile move, EL7041-0052 Stepper open loop + autosave restore Stepper open loop + retries Stepper without motor record Servo CSV Hardware substitution template  Synchronization examples  Slit synchronization Mirror synchronization  PLC and general examples  Basic PLC examples Master-less PLC example Motion sequence PLC example Data storage buffer  Simulation and hardware acceptance fixtures The dedicated slit setup lives alongside its runners in this repository:
   Purpose Repository path     Memory-backed slit IOC tests/integration/slit/ioc/startup.cmd   External plant and simulation cases tests/integration/slit/run.py   Real-hardware slit IOC tests/integration/slit/ioc_hardware/startup.cmd   Real-hardware acceptance cases tests/integration/slit_hardware/run.py   Offline simulator/harness checks (no IOC) python3 tests/run_simulation_checks.py    See Simulation backend and the two runner READMEs for setup and case selection. The simulation runner requires a SIM IOC; it injects feedback and faults. The hardware runner checks a separate hardware fixture and performs real motion. Hardware homing is an explicit separate group, excluded from its default run.
Legacy ESS examples The examples/ESS/ tree is mainly useful when reading or maintaining older classic motion configurations based on .ax, .vax, and .sax files.
See legacy motion for the corresponding manual page.
Notes  Prefer addSlave.cmd together with applyComponent.cmd for slave and component setup. Prefer loadYamlAxis.cmd for axes. Prefer loadYamlPlc.cmd or loadPLCFile.cmd for PLCs. Keep drive SDO verification enabled, and configure unused channels with Generic-Ch-Not-Used.

title: Upgrades
content:
Purpose Collect upgrade notes and migration checklists for major versions.
Release Notes New features are described in ecmc RELEASE.md: https://github.com/epics-modules/ecmc/blob/master/RELEASE.md
v10 -> v11 Highlights  CSP-PC mode added (centralized position loop in CSP) Position-velocity-time (profile move) support Motor record PID fields still limited to 0..1.0; use values 100x smaller than native ecmc settings  Be careful when using motor record PID fields.
Example: ecmc Kp=1.0 corresponds to motor record PCOF=0.01.
 Breaking Changes in v11  getAxisStatusStructV2 removed (plugins need rebuild) Event*, CommandList*, DataRecorder* removed (replace with PLC logic) Motor record MtnCmd mbbo indices changed (prefer string writes, or update index-based clients)  Migration Checklist (v10 -> v11)  Auto-enable: move from motor record parameters to axis.autoEnable in YAML Master/slave synchronization: replace PLC state machine logic with native addMasterSlaveSM.cmd Limit logic: use plcOverride and write ax<id>.mon.lowlim/highlim in PLC code Drive safety: ensure SDO verification is executed for every used drive channel  Auto-enable (recommended migration) Remove legacy motor-record auto-enable parameter strings:
# remove legacy: # parameters: 'powerAutoOnOff=2;powerOffDelay=-1;' Use native ecmc auto-enable:
axis: autoEnable: enableTimeout: 1.0 disableTimeout: 5.0 atStartup: false Native master/slave state machine For virtual/physical synchronized systems, replace PLC-side state machine code with addMasterSlaveSM.cmd:
${SCRIPTEXEC} ${ecmccfg_DIR}addMasterSlaveSM.cmd "NAME=Slit_SM, MST_GRP_NAME=virtualAxes, SLV_GRP_NAME=realAxes" If you have multiple systems, use unique NAME, MST_GRP_NAME, and SLV_GRP_NAME per system.
For the runtime PVs and the normal setup pattern, see Master/Slave State Machine.
Limit logic via plcOverride Use plcOverride in YAML and compute limits in PLC logic:
input: limit: forward: 'plcOverride' backward: 'plcOverride' plc: enable: true externalCommands: true code: - ax${AX_ID=1}.mon.lowlim:=ec_chk_bit(ec0.s$(DRV_SID).binaryInputs01,0) and ec_chk_bit(ec0.s$(DRV_SID).ONE,0); - ax${AX_ID=1}.mon.highlim:=ec_chk_bit(ec0.s$(DRV_SID).binaryInputs01,1) and ec_chk_bit(ec0.s$(DRV_SID).ONE,1); SDO verification for drives v11 adds SDO verification workflow checks (mainly stepper/servo drives):
 addSlave.cmd marks drive channels that require SDO setup. applyComponent.cmd marks channels as configured after component application. Validation before iocInit fails if required channels are missing SDO configuration.  If a multi-channel drive has an unused channel, still configure it (for example Generic-Ch-Not-Used).
